rules.relevance: Distinguished on facts as it involved a finding of no debtor-creditor relationship and did not rely on the larger bench decision in Chunchun Jha.

rules.reference: Transfer of Property Act, 1882
rules.relevance: Defines a mortgage as a transfer of interest to secure payment of money advanced or a debt, establishing the necessity of a debtor-creditor relationship.

rules.case_name: Shri Bhaskar Waman Joshi v. Shri Narayan Rambilas Agarwal
rules.reference: Shri Bhaskar Waman Joshi v. Shri Narayan Rambilas Agarwal
rules.relevance: Held that a mortgage by conditional sale creates a debtor-creditor relationship where the price is charged on the property, distinguishing it from a sale with an option to repurchase.

rules.reference: Transfer of Property Act, 1882
rules.relevance: The court held that where ownership passes before full payment, the seller is entitled to a statutory charge on the property for the unpaid amount, rendering the sale valid despite non-payment.

rules.case_name: Rohitbhai Jivanlal Patel v. State of Gujarat
rules.reference: Rohitbhai Jivanlal Patel v. State of Gujarat
rules.relevance: Establishes that once the signature is proved, the onus shifts to the accused to rebut the presumption under Section 139, and the court cannot question the complainant's evidence on source of funds.

rules.case_name: Gamini Bala Koteswara Rao and others Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh through Secretary
rules.reference: Gamini Bala Koteswara Rao and others Vs. State of Andhra Pradesh through Secretary
rules.relevance: Defined 'perverse' as against the weight of evidence, limiting appellate interference with acquittals.

rules.case_name: Reverend Mother Marykutty vs. Reni C. Kottaram & Anr.
rules.reference: Reverend Mother Marykutty vs. Reni C. Kottaram & Anr.
rules.relevance: Establishes that the presumption under Section 139 is rebuttable by raising a probable defence based on preponderance of probabilities.

rules.case_name: Kali Ram Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh
rules.reference: Kali Ram Vs. State of Himachal Pradesh
rules.relevance: Held that the burden on an accused to rebut a statutory presumption is not as heavy as the prosecution's burden; material consistent with innocence entitles the accused to acquittal.

rules.case_name: Sunil Todi v. State of Gujarat
rules.reference: Sunil Todi v. State of Gujarat
rules.relevance: Clarified that 'debt or other liability' includes debts incurred after drawing but before encashment, and emphasized the need for a legally enforceable debt at the time of encashment.

rules.reference: Distinction between framing of charge and summoning under Section 319
rules.relevance: The court distinguished the standard for framing charges (where strong suspicion based on investigation materials may suffice) from summoning under Section 319 (which requires satisfaction based on fresh evidence brought on record during trial).

rules.case_name: Guriya alias Tabassum Tauquir and Others v. State of Bihar and Another
rules.reference: Guriya alias Tabassum Tauquir v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: Held that mere mention of names in an FIR or protest petition without attribution of overt acts is insufficient to justify summoning under Section 319.

rules.case_name: Y. Saraba Reddy v. Puthur Sani Reddy and Another
rules.reference: Y. Saraba Reddy v. Puthur Sani Reddy
rules.relevance: Held that the court must analyze the evidence of witnesses rather than relying on the satisfaction of the investigating officer when deciding to summon an accused under Section 319.

rules.case_name: Joginder Singh & Anr. v. State of Punjab & Anr.
rules.reference: Joginder Singh & Anr. v. State of Punjab & Anr.
rules.relevance: Established that a Court can add any person not accused before it as an accused if sufficient evidence indicates involvement during trial.

rules.case_name: Rakesh & Anr. v. State of Haryana
rules.reference: Rakesh & Anr. v. State of Haryana
rules.relevance: Held that 'evidence' in Section 319 is comprehensive and includes prima facie material from examination-in-chief, allowing the power to be exercised before cross-examination is complete.

rules.reference: Adverse possession requires denial of title
rules.relevance: The court relied on concurrent findings that the defendants did not deny the plaintiffs' title until 1976, thus adverse possession had not commenced.

rules.case_name: Venkataraja and Ors. vs. Vidyane Doureradjaperumal (Dead) Through Legal Representatives and Ors.
rules.reference: Venkataraja and Ors. vs. Vidyane Doureradjaperumal (Dead) Through Legal Representatives and Ors.
rules.relevance: Relied on to clarify that while amendment to include unsought relief is permissible, it must be saved by limitation, supporting the rejection of the late amendment for possession.

rules.reference: Limitation Act, 1963
rules.relevance: The court interpreted this provision to hold that it applies only when the plaintiff's right is independent of the deceased female's right, not when derived from a female who was the absolute owner.

rules.case_name: Sri Aralappa vs. Sri Jagannath & others
rules.reference: Sri Aralappa vs. Sri Jagannath & others
rules.relevance: The Supreme Court disagreed with the ratio of this High Court decision, holding that a suit is not dismissible as not maintainable merely because the plaintiff fails to prove possession for the injunction, provided the plaint claimed both declaration and injunction.

rules.reference: Presumption that possession follows title
rules.relevance: The court considered this principle but held it inapplicable because the plaintiff had admitted in the earlier suit that the defendant was in possession and cultivation.

rules.reference: Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957
rules.relevance: Mandates that any person having authority to receive evidence must examine instruments to ascertain if they are duly stamped and impound them if they are not.

rules.reference: Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957
rules.relevance: The court interpreted this section to hold that the penalty for insufficiently stamped instruments is mandatory at 10 times the deficient duty, leaving no discretion to the trial court.

rules.case_name: Digambar Warty and others vs. District Registrar, Bangalore Urban District and another
rules.reference: Digambar Warty and others vs. District Registrar, Bangalore Urban District and another
rules.relevance: The court relied on this Division Bench judgment to uphold the view that trial courts have no discretion to reduce the statutory penalty of 10 times under Section 34.

rules.reference: Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957
rules.relevance: The court contrasted this section with Section 34 to highlight that discretion to impose lesser penalties is vested in the Deputy Commissioner, not the trial court.

rules.reference: Karnataka Stamp Act, 1957
rules.relevance: The court noted that this section empowers the Deputy Commissioner to refund penalty if he thinks fit, indicating legislative intent that 10 times penalty need not always be realized.

rules.reference: Statement on Industrial Policy, 1991
rules.relevance: Guidelines for foreign investment approval, specifically regarding access to high technology and world markets, used to validate YKK's approval.

rules.reference: Industries (Development and Regulation) Act, 1951
rules.relevance: Empowers the Central Government to constitute an Advisory Committee to determine articles reserved for small-scale industry, forming the basis for the dereservation notification.

rules.case_name: D. Navinchandra & Co. v. Union of India
rules.reference: D. Navinchandra & Co. v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Confirmed that rights under Additional licences are governed by the terms of the import policy prevailing at the time of import and that canalisation policies remain applicable.

rules.reference: Judicial non-interference in economic policy
rules.relevance: Courts should not interfere with government economic policy unless it is contrary to the Constitution or wholly arbitrary.

rules.case_name: State of Bihar v. Kripalu Shanker
rules.reference: State of Bihar v. Kripalu Shanker
rules.relevance: Established that internal notes by officers or Ministers cannot be used to alter an approval already granted.

rules.reference: Graduate Medical Education Regulations, 1997 (as amended by MCI notification dated 04.02.2019)
rules.relevance: Establishes the essential eligibility criteria for PwD admission to MBBS, requiring 40% benchmark disability and specific physical capabilities regarding hands.

rules.reference: Relevant date for eligibility criteria
rules.relevance: The court determined that the relevant date for applying eligibility criteria is when candidates seek admission and appear before the Medical Board, not when the selection brochure is released.

rules.case_name: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India
rules.reference: Janhit Abhiyan v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Petitioners relied on this case to argue against mid-process rule changes; the court distinguished it by noting the amendment was published before the actual admission process for 2019-20 commenced.

rules.reference: Right of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
rules.relevance: Provides the statutory basis for 5% reservation in government educational institutions for persons with benchmark disability.

rules.case_name: Vikash Kumar v. Union Public Service Commission
rules.reference: Vikash Kumar v. Union Public Service Commission
rules.relevance: Established that reasonable accommodation is a fundamental right and that facilities for PwD should not be restricted only to those with benchmark disabilities, except for reservation quotas.

rules.case_name: Mewa Ram & Another v. State of Rajasthan
rules.reference: Mewa Ram & Another v. State of Rajasthan
rules.relevance: Held that exhortation to kill a specific person does not establish common intention to kill a different person unless there is evidence linking the accused to the specific killing.

rules.case_name: Shobhit Chamar & Another v. State of Bihar
rules.reference: Shobhit Chamar & Another v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: Held that a challenge to conviction based on non-compliance of Section 313 CrPC raised for the first time in appeal cannot be entertained unless prejudice is demonstrated.

rules.case_name: Pandurang Tukia and Bhillia v. State of Hyderabad
rules.reference: Pandurang Tukia and Bhillia v. State of Hyderabad
rules.relevance: Established that common intention presupposes prior concert or a pre-arranged plan, which can be formed suddenly on the spot.

rules.case_name: Santosh Kumar Singh v. State through CBI
rules.reference: Santosh Kumar Singh v. State through CBI
rules.relevance: Reiterated that omission to put material circumstances does not automatically exclude evidence unless prejudice and miscarriage of justice are shown.

rules.case_name: S. Harnam Singh v. State (Delhi Admn.)
rules.reference: S. Harnam Singh v. State (Delhi Admn.)
rules.relevance: Held that each material circumstance must be put to the accused specifically and distinctly; failure to do so is a serious irregularity vitiating the trial if prejudice is shown.

rules.case_name: Executive Engineer, Dhenkanal Minor Irrigation Division, Orissa & Ors. Vs. N. C. Budharaj
rules.reference: Executive Engineer, Dhenkanal Minor Irrigation Division, Orissa & Ors. Vs. N. C. Budharaj
rules.relevance: Holds that an arbitrator has jurisdiction to award pre-reference interest unless there is a specific stipulation or prohibition in the contract.

rules.reference: Effect of Express Prohibition on Arbitrator's Power
rules.relevance: An express contractual clause barring interest 'for any reason whatsoever' restricts the arbitrator's inherent power to award pre-reference and pendente lite interest for the period covered by the agreement.

rules.case_name: Food Corporation of India vs. Mis. A. M. Ahmed & Co. & Anr.
rules.reference: Food Corporation of India vs. Mis. A. M. Ahmed & Co. & Anr.
rules.relevance: Confirms that escalation due to statutory wage revision is a normal incident of contracts and within the arbitrator's jurisdiction to award.

rules.reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
rules.relevance: Allows setting aside an award if it deals with a dispute not contemplated by or not falling within the terms of the submission to arbitration.

rules.case_name: Tarapore & Co. vs. State of M.P.
rules.reference: Tarapore & Co. vs. State of M.P.
rules.relevance: Establishes that if a contractor is required to pay fair wages as per subsequent statutory notifications, the State is impliedly bound to reimburse the increased payment, even without an explicit escalation clause.

rules.case_name: Mademsetty Satyanarayana v. G. Yelloji Rao and others
rules.reference: Mademsetty Satyanarayana v. G. Yelloji Rao and others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to establish that in India, specific performance is a statutory right, and mere delay cannot be a ground for refusing relief if the suit is filed within the period of limitation.

rules.reference: Deemed Service of Registered Letters
rules.relevance: The court applied the principle that a registered letter sent to the correct address is deemed served even if returned, unless the contrary is proved, to establish the plaintiff's notice to the defendant.

rules.case_name: Smt. Chand Rani (dead) by LRs. Vs. Smt. Kamal Rani(dead) by LRs
rules.reference: Smt. Chand Rani (dead) by LRs. Vs. Smt. Kamal Rani(dead) by LRs
rules.relevance: Held that while time is generally not the essence of a contract for immovable property, parties can agree to make it so, and such intention must be expressed in unequivocal language.

rules.reference: Time is of the essence of the contract
rules.relevance: The court determined that despite the general presumption in immovable property sales, the express terms and surrounding circumstances made time of the essence for the payment of Rs. 4 lakhs.

rules.case_name: Chand Rani (Smt.) (Dead) by Lrs. v. Kamal Rani (Smt.) (Dead) by Lrs.
rules.reference: Chand Rani (Smt.) (Dead) by Lrs. v. Kamal Rani (Smt.) (Dead) by Lrs.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to establish that specific performance can be denied if the purchaser is not ready and willing to pay within the stipulated time, especially when time is of the essence.

rules.reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
rules.relevance: Defines the limited grounds for setting aside an arbitral award, including disputes not contemplated by the submission to arbitration and matters not capable of settlement by arbitration.

rules.case_name: Bhaskar Industrial Development Limited v. South Western Railway
rules.reference: Bhaskar Industrial Development Limited v. South Western Railway
rules.relevance: Expounded that the power of the Court under Section 34 is not to remand the matter to the Arbitral Tribunal after setting aside the arbitral award.

rules.case_name: McDermott International Inc. v. Burn Standard Co. Ltd.
rules.reference: McDermott International Inc. v. Burn Standard Co. Ltd.
rules.relevance: Established that Parliament has not conferred any power of remand to the Court to remit the matter to the arbitral tribunal except to adjourn proceedings as provided under Section 34(4).

rules.case_name: MMTC v. Vicnivass Agency
rules.reference: MMTC v. Vicnivass Agency
rules.relevance: Clarified that Section 34(4) requires a request from a party and that the court's powers are limited to setting aside or adjourning, not remanding after setting aside.

rules.case_name: M/s. Deep Industries Limited v. Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited
rules.reference: M/s. Deep Industries Limited v. Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited
rules.relevance: Relied on for the interplay between Section 5 of the Arbitration Act and Article 227, and the procedure that challenges to Section 16 orders must await the final award under Section 34.

rules.reference: Indian Succession Act, 1925
rules.relevance: The court interpreted this provision to hold that an attesting witness must personally sign or affix a mark, and cannot delegate this act to another person, unlike the testator who may direct another to sign.

rules.case_name: Seth Beni Chand v. Smt. Kamla Kunwar & Ors.
rules.reference: Seth Beni Chand v. Smt. Kamla Kunwar & Ors.
rules.relevance: Confirmed that the onus probandi lies on the propounder to satisfy the court that the Will is the last will of a free and capable testator.

rules.case_name: V. Kalyanaswamy (D) by L.Rs. & Ors. v L. Bakthavatsalam (D) by L.Rs. & Ors.
rules.reference: V. Kalyanaswamy (D) by L.Rs. & Ors. v L. Bakthavatsalam (D) by L.Rs. & Ors.
rules.relevance: Clarified that under Section 69, it is sufficient to prove the handwriting of the testator and one attesting witness, dispensing with the requirement of Section 68 to examine an attesting witness.

rules.case_name: H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B.F.N. Thimmajamma
rules.reference: H. Venkatachala Iyengar v. B.F.N. Thimmajamma
rules.relevance: Established that the propounder must prove the testator's sound disposing mind, understanding of dispositions, and free will, and must remove any suspicious circumstances.

rules.case_name: Dauat Ram v. Sodha
rules.reference: Dauat Ram v. Sodha
rules.relevance: Confirmed that a will must be proved by primary evidence and that the propounder must satisfy the requirements of Sections 63 and 68, including proving the testator signed in the presence of witnesses who attested in his presence.

rules.case_name: In re The Delhi Laws Act
rules.reference: In re The Delhi Laws Act
rules.relevance: Established the principle that delegation of essential legislative functions is invalid.

rules.reference: Calcutta Municipal Act, 1951
rules.relevance: Authorized the Corporation to charge a fee for licences at rates fixed by the Corporation.

rules.case_name: Western India Theatres Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Poona
rules.reference: Western India Theatres Ltd. v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Poona
rules.relevance: Held that power to impose taxes for the purposes of the Act furnishes sufficient guidance for delegation.

rules.case_name: Pandit Benarsi Das Bhanot v. The State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.reference: Pandit Benarsi Das Bhanot v. The State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.relevance: Held that it is not unconstitutional to leave details of taxation laws, such as rates, to the executive if guidance is provided.

rules.case_name: The Hingir-Rampur Coal Co. Ltd. v. The State of Orissa and ors.
rules.reference: The Hingir-Rampur Coal Co. Ltd. v. The State of Orissa and ors.
rules.relevance: Held that a levy is a fee if the special service rendered is distinctly and primarily meant for the benefit of a specified class.

rules.reference: Electricity Act, 2003

rules.reference: Disobedience to statutory orders

rules.reference: Circular No. 477 dated 29.10.2002 (General Terms and Conditions of Supply)
rules.relevance: Provides that if supply remains disconnected for three months, the agreement is deemed terminated, and the consumer is liable for minimum charges only for that three-month period.

rules.reference: Bona fide dispute and willingness to pay
rules.relevance: Non-payment in the context of a bona fide dispute or a demonstrated willingness to pay (e.g., via instalment requests) does not constitute 'neglect to pay' under Section 56.

rules.case_name: Corporation of the City of Nagpur Vs. Nagpur Electric Light and Power Company Limited
rules.reference: Corporation of the City of Nagpur Vs. Nagpur Electric Light and Power Company Limited
rules.relevance: Supports the view that non-payment due to a bona fide dispute on quantum of dues does not amount to negligence to pay.

rules.case_name: Ghanashyam Mishra & Sons Private Limited v. Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company Limited

rules.case_name: Supertech Limited v. Emerald Court Owner Resident Welfare Association & Others

rules.reference: Supreme Court Rules, 1966
rules.relevance: Prohibits filing a second review application after a previous review has been disposed of.

rules.reference: Nature of Contempt Proceedings
rules.relevance: Contempt is an offence against the dignity of the Court, not a private wrong; therefore, the decision to proceed or withdraw lies with the Court based on whether respect for the judicial process is enhanced or dwindled.

rules.case_name: Supertech Limited vs. Emerald Court Owner Resident Welfare Association
rules.reference: Supertech Limited vs. Emerald Court Owner Resident Welfare Association
rules.relevance: Deprecated the practice of filing miscellaneous applications in disposed appeals to modify judgments or avoid compliance, stating one cannot do indirectly what one cannot do directly.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908

rules.case_name: Ahuja Industries Ltd. v. State of Karnataka

rules.reference: The Rajasthan Tenancy Act, 1955

rules.case_name: Anurag Soni v. State of Chhattisgarh

rules.reference: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860

rules.reference: Essential Commodities Act, 1955

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860

rules.reference: FIR is not encyclopedic

rules.case_name: Aneeta Hada v. Godfather Travels and Tours Private Ltd.

rules.reference: Aneeta Hada v. Godfather Travels & Tours Private Limited
rules.relevance: Held that arraigning the company as an accused is imperative for maintaining prosecution against its signatories under Section 141.

rules.case_name: Raghbans Dubey v. State of Bihar

rules.relevance: Distinguished the general CrPC principle that cognizance is of the offence not the offender, holding it inapplicable to the person-specific nature of offences under the NI Act.

rules.case_name: State of Karnataka v. Pratap Chand and Others

rules.relevance: Held that a partner is not vicariously liable merely by virtue of being a partner; prosecution must prove they were in charge of and responsible for the conduct of business.

rules.case_name: State of Rajasthan v. Shera Ram alias Vishnu Dutta

rules.case_name: State of Rajasthan vs. Teja Ram & Ors.

rules.case_name: C. Muniappan & Ors. vs. State of Tamil Nadu

rules.case_name: Santosh Devi vs. National Insurance Company Ltd. and Others

rules.case_name: Rajesh and Others vs. Rajbir Singh and Others

rules.case_name: Master Ayush v. Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Another

rules.relevance: Supports the award of compensation for loss of marriage prospects and conveyance charges in cases involving severe disability and young victims.

rules.reference: Demolition of unauthorized constructions in flagrant violation of plans

rules.case_name: Kanpur University, Through Vice Chancellor and Others v. Samir Gupta and Ors.

rules.case_name: Guru Nanak Dev University v. Saumil Garg and others

rules.case_name: Writ Petition (C) No. 390 of 2017

rules.relevance: Appellate forums must examine evidence in totality. A Medical Council report is relevant but not determinative, particularly when it contradicts uncontroverted expert evidence presented in the consumer forum.

rules.reference: Duty of care in medical services
rules.relevance: The court affirmed that the duty of care in medical services does not end with surgery but extends to pre-operative and post-operative care, especially in complex cases.

rules.case_name: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab and Another
rules.reference: Jacob Mathew v. State of Punjab and Another
rules.relevance: Established that simple lack of care, error of judgment, or accident is not proof of negligence; a doctor is liable only if they lack requisite skills or do not exercise reasonable competence.

rules.case_name: M.A Biviji v. Sunita & Ors.
rules.reference: M.A Biviji v. Sunita & Ors.
rules.relevance: Cited for the three essential ingredients of medical negligence: duty of care, breach of duty, and resulting damage.

rules.case_name: Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences v. Prasanth S. Dhananka
rules.reference: Nizam’s Institute of Medical Sciences v. Prasanth S. Dhananka
rules.relevance: Established that compensation must strike a balance between the victim's demands and the liable party's interests, and that injured persons often suffer more distress than those who die.

rules.case_name: Paramjeet Singh alias Pamma v. State of Uttarakhand
rules.reference: Paramjeet Singh alias Pamma v. State of Uttarakhand
rules.relevance: Establishes that an accused can be convicted only on legal evidence, not surmises, regardless of the offence's gruesomeness.

rules.case_name: Kunju Muhammed alias Khumani v. State of Kerala
rules.reference: Kunju Muhammed alias Khumani v. State of Kerala
rules.relevance: Holds that if a witness is not declared hostile but their evidence helps the defense, the benefit should go to the accused.

rules.case_name: Suraj Mal v. State (Delhi Administration)
rules.reference: Suraj Mal v. State (Delhi Administration)
rules.relevance: Holds that testimony of witnesses making inconsistent statements is unreliable and unworthy of credence.

rules.case_name: State of U.P. v. Shambhu Nath Singh
rules.reference: State of U.P. v. Shambhu Nath Singh
rules.relevance: Reinforces the mandate under Section 309 Cr.P.C. for day-to-day trials and criticizes flippant adjournments.

rules.reference: Burden of proof regarding recovered stolen property
rules.relevance: The court held that recovery of cash is insignificant if the prosecution fails to prove the specific amount was carried by the victim and that the recovered amount is the same looted money.

rules.reference: Exceptional Circumstances for CBI Investigation
rules.relevance: The court articulated that CBI investigation can be directed in exceptional situations to provide credibility, instill confidence, or do complete justice, even if national/international ramifications are absent.

rules.case_name: Committee for Protection of Democratic Rights, West Bengal & Ors. vs. Union of India & Ors.
rules.reference: Committee for Protection of Democratic Rights, West Bengal & Ors. vs. Union of India & Ors.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this case to establish that constitutional courts have the power to direct CBI investigation in exceptional situations to ensure credibility and enforce fundamental rights, even without State consent.

rules.reference: Academic Nature of 'First FIR' Controversy
rules.relevance: The court held that when a single common agency (CBI) is directed to investigate all FIRs, the question of which FIR was the 'first' becomes academic and does not bar the investigation.

rules.case_name: Kari Choudhary v. Most. Sita Devi and Ors.
rules.reference: Kari Choudhary v. Most. Sita Devi and Ors.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment for the principle that rival versions of the same incident can result in two different FIRs investigated by the same agency, and that quashing proceedings merely because a final report was laid in the first FIR is too technical.

rules.case_name: Bhaurati Tanung vs. Union of India & Ors.
rules.reference: Bhaurati Tanung vs. Union of India & Ors.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this case as it involved similar facts (murder of a political leader) and supported the direction for de novo investigation by CBI to ensure complete justice.

rules.reference: State Bank of India Officers' Service Rules, 1992 (SBIOSR)
rules.relevance: Allows continuation of disciplinary proceedings after superannuation if initiated before cessation of service. The court held this rule inapplicable as proceedings had already concluded.

rules.reference: State Bank of India Officers' Service Rules, 1992 (SBIOSR)
rules.relevance: Defines the age of superannuation and the discretion to extend service. The court analyzed this to determine the respondent's service status.

rules.case_name: State Bank of India & Ors. v. Kamal Kishore Prasad
rules.citation: Order dated 25.11.2013 in SLP (C) No. 16541 of 2010
rules.reference: State Bank of India & Ors. v. Kamal Kishore Prasad
rules.relevance: The Supreme Court's earlier order in the same matter directed the Appointing Authority to take an appropriate decision keeping all contentions open, which formed the basis for the fresh proceedings.

rules.case_name: Canara Bank v. D.R.P. Sundharam
rules.reference: Canara Bank v. D.R.P. Sundharam
rules.relevance: A three-Judge Bench upheld the view in Rajender Lal Capoor, reiterating that a disciplinary proceeding initiated by means of a charge-sheet prior to retirement continues after retirement, but a show cause notice alone is insufficient.

rules.reference: Principle of Natural Justice / Administrative Law
rules.relevance: The principle that the person who hears the matter must pass the order was relied upon to validate the Appointing Authority's fresh decision.

rules.reference: Value of Medical Evidence
rules.relevance: Medical evidence is corroborative; it cannot override credible eyewitness testimony unless it completely rules out the possibility of the alleged manner of injury.

rules.case_name: Mafabhai Nagarbhai Raval v. State of Gujarat
rules.reference: Mafabhai Nagarbhai Raval v. State of Gujarat
rules.relevance: Held that a person suffering 99% burn injuries can be deemed capable of making a dying declaration unless there is an inherent defect.

rules.case_name: Sher Singh & Anr. v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Sher Singh & Anr. v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: Held that a subsequent declaration can be preferred over an earlier involuntary one, and absence of a doctor's certificate is not fatal if the recorder is satisfied of fitness.

rules.case_name: Bhiny Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar
rules.reference: Bhiny Kumar Singh v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: Established that the burden of proving an alibi lies heavily on the accused, requiring proof with absolute certainty to exclude the possibility of presence at the scene.

rules.case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Dal Singh and Others
rules.reference: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Dal Singh and Others
rules.relevance: Supported reliance on a dying declaration of a deceased who suffered 100% burn injuries.

rules.case_name: Consumer Education & Research Centre and others v. Union of India and others
rules.reference: Consumer Education & Research Centre and others v. Union of India and others
rules.relevance: Held that the right to health and medical care to protect one's health and vigour while in service is a fundamental right under Article 21 read with Articles 39(e), 41, 43, and 48-A.

rules.reference: Constitution of India
rules.relevance: Directive Principles of State Policy that support the right to health, protection of workers' strength, just and humane conditions of work, and environmental protection, giving life breath to Article 21.

rules.case_name: People’s Union for Democratic Rights v. Union of India
rules.reference: People’s Union for Democratic Rights v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Relied on for the interpretation of Article 23, establishing that lack of minimum safety standards constitutes forced labour and consent is irrelevant in cases of economic helplessness.

rules.reference: State Obligation in Hazardous Jobs
rules.relevance: The State's duty to provide minimum conditions for human dignity is doubled when workers are engaged in hazardous and risky jobs.

rules.reference: Constitution of India
rules.relevance: These Directive Principles mandate the State to secure the health and strength of workers, ensure just and humane conditions of work, and protect the environment, giving life-breath to the right to dignity under Article 21.

rules.reference: Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodity) Rules, 1977
rules.relevance: Exempts packages containing commodities of 10 grams or less (sold by weight/measure) from the requirement to declare retail sale price.

rules.case_name: Jayanti Food Processing (P) Ltd. v. Commissioner of C.Ex., Rajasthan
rules.reference: Jayanti Food Processing (P) Ltd. v. Commissioner of C.Ex., Rajasthan
rules.relevance: Established that MRP declaration is required only for packages meant for retail sale to the ultimate consumer.

rules.reference: Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodity) Rules, 1977
rules.relevance: Permits cosmetics (Item 25 of Schedule V) to be sold by weight or measure, requiring quantity declaration in terms of mass.

rules.reference: Standards of Weights and Measures (Packaged Commodity) Rules, 1977
rules.relevance: Defines 'multi-piece package' as a package containing two or more individually packaged pieces of the same commodity.

rules.case_name: Varnica Herbs vs. C.B.E.&C., New Delhi
rules.reference: Varnica Herbs vs. C.B.E.&C., New Delhi
rules.relevance: Held that Rule 34 exemption does not apply to multi-piece packages; the Supreme Court held this decision per incuriam.

rules.reference: Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940
rules.relevance: Empowers the Central Government to prohibit the manufacture and sale of drugs if satisfied that they involve risk to human beings or lack therapeutic justification.

rules.case_name: State of Madras v. V.G. Row
rules.reference: State of Madras v. V.G. Row
rules.relevance: Establishes criteria for examining the reasonableness of restrictions under Article 19, including the nature of the right, purpose of restriction, and extent of the evil.

rules.reference: Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940
rules.relevance: Empowers the Central Government to constitute the Drugs Consultative Committee to advise on securing uniformity in administration.

rules.case_name: Ishwari Khetan Sugar Mills (P) Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh
rules.reference: Ishwari Khetan Sugar Mills (P) Ltd. v. State of Uttar Pradesh
rules.relevance: Relied on to hold that State legislative power is eroded only to the extent of control assumed by the Union over declared industries.

rules.reference: Drugs & Cosmetics Act, 1940
rules.relevance: Provides for the constitution of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board to advise the government on technical matters.

rules.case_name: Balasaria Construction (P) Ltd. v. Hanuman Seva Trust & Ors.
rules.reference: Balasaria Construction (P) Ltd. v. Hanuman Seva Trust & Ors.
rules.relevance: Held that a plaint cannot be rejected under Order VII Rule 11(d) if the suit is not ex facie barred by limitation, as limitation is a mixed question of fact and law.

rules.case_name: Popat and Kotecha Property v. State Bank of India Staff Association
rules.reference: Popat and Kotecha Property v. State Bank of India Staff Association
rules.relevance: Established that Order VII Rule 11(d) is not applicable if the question of limitation involves mixed questions of fact and law requiring evidence, and that the plaint must show on its face that it is barred by law.

rules.case_name: Nusli Neville Wadia v. Ivory Properties and Others
rules.reference: Nusli Neville Wadia v. Ivory Properties and Others
rules.relevance: Held that limitation is a mixed question of law and fact and cannot be decided as a preliminary issue under Order XIV Rule 2 unless facts are admitted.

rules.case_name: Church of Christ Charitable Trust and Educational Charitable Society Vs. Ponniamman Educational Trust
rules.reference: Church of Christ Charitable Trust and Educational Charitable Society Vs. Ponniamman Educational Trust
rules.relevance: Reiterated the principle that the court must scrutinize only the averments in the plaint and cannot rely on external evidence or defendant's defenses at the stage of deciding an application under Order VII Rule 11.

rules.case_name: Balasaria Construction (P) Ltd. v. Hanuman Seva Trust and Others
rules.reference: Balasaria Construction (P) Ltd. v. Hanuman Seva Trust and Others
rules.relevance: Held that a plaint cannot be rejected under Order VII, Rule 11(d) for issues like limitation or bar by law if they involve mixed questions of law and fact requiring evidence.

rules.case_name: State of Kerala and others Vs. Rajesh and others
rules.reference: State of Kerala and others Vs. Rajesh and others
rules.relevance: Reinforced that 'reasonable grounds' requires facts sufficient to justify satisfaction of innocence, criticizing liberal approaches to bail under the NDPS Act.

rules.case_name: Tofan Singh v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: Tofan Singh v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.relevance: Held that confessional statements under Section 67 are inadmissible in trial, but did not negate the relevance of disclosures leading to recovery.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. Thamisharasi and Ors.
rules.reference: Union of India v. Thamisharasi and Ors.
rules.relevance: Established that the twin conditions under Section 37(1)(b) are cumulative and require 'reasonable grounds' which mean something more than prima facie grounds, contemplating substantial probable causes.

rules.case_name: Union of India and Ors. v. Jaipal Singh
rules.reference: Union of India and Ors. v. Jaipal Singh
rules.relevance: Held that an order passed in an SLP at the threshold without detailed reasons does not constitute a declaration of law or a binding precedent.

rules.case_name: Collector of Customs, New Delhi v. Ahmadalieva Nodira
rules.reference: Collector of Customs, New Delhi v. Ahmadalieva Nodira
rules.relevance: Clarified that the twin conditions under Section 37(1)(b) are cumulative and that 'reasonable grounds' requires substantial probable causes for believing the accused is not guilty, which is a higher standard than prima facie grounds.

rules.reference: Criminal law is not akin to money recovery proceedings
rules.relevance: The court relied on the principle that criminal proceedings cannot be utilized for 'arm-twisting' or money recovery, and bail decisions must be based on material on record rather than payment offers.

rules.reference: Jail is the rule and bail is an exception for money launderers
rules.relevance: In cases of money laundering and economic offences affecting national interest, the presumption is against granting bail.

rules.case_name: Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy v. Central Bureau of Investigation
rules.reference: Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy v. Central Bureau of Investigation
rules.relevance: Held that economic offences involving deep-rooted conspiracies and huge loss of public funds pose a serious threat to the national economy and must be viewed seriously.

rules.case_name: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
rules.reference: Arnesh Kumar v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: Laid down mandatory directions to prevent mechanical arrests in Section 498A IPC cases and emphasized the necessity of recording reasons for arrest.

rules.case_name: State of U.P. vs. Amarmani Tripathi
rules.reference: State of U.P. vs. Amarmani Tripathi
rules.relevance: Distinguished between appeals against bail and applications for cancellation; clarified that while post-bail conduct is relevant for cancellation, it is not the sole ground, and superior courts can cancel bail if the granting court acted on irrelevant material or with manifest impropriety.

rules.case_name: State of Haryana and Another Vs. Sandeep Singh and Others
rules.reference: State of Haryana and Another Vs. Sandeep Singh and Others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to interpret the Haryana School Education Service Rules, 2012, holding that the conversion of PTI posts to TGT did not extinguish the requirement for fresh selection under the earlier advertisement.

rules.case_name: Tamil Nadu Computer Science BED Graduate Teachers Welfare Society(1) vs. Higher Secondary School Computer Teachers Association and others
rules.reference: Tamil Nadu Computer Science BED Graduate Teachers Welfare Society(1) vs. Higher Secondary School Computer Teachers Association and others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this case to hold that changing qualifying norms or criteria at the verge of the end of the selection process is arbitrary and unjustified.

rules.case_name: Lila Dhar vs. State of Rajasthan and others
rules.reference: Lila Dhar vs. State of Rajasthan and others
rules.relevance: The court cited this judgment for the principle that the object of selection is to secure the best and most suitable person through merit-based open competition.

rules.case_name: Bishnu Biswas and others Union of India and others
rules.reference: Bishnu Biswas and others Union of India and others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this case to support the view that changing rules of the game during the selection process indicates lack of transparency and is impermissible.

rules.case_name: Ratnagiri Gas and Power Private Limited Vs. RDS Projects Limited and Others
rules.reference: Ratnagiri Gas and Power Private Limited Vs. RDS Projects Limited and Others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this case to distinguish between 'malice in fact' and 'malice in law', holding that the present case involved malice in law (arbitrary action) rather than personal malice.

rules.case_name: PEPSU Road Transport Corporation, Patiala v. Mangat Singh and Ors.
rules.reference: PEPSU Road Transport Corporation, Patiala v. Mangat Singh and Ors.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to support the plea of delay and laches, noting that accepting CPF benefits extinguishes further legal rights.

rules.case_name: D.R. Gurushantappa v. Abdul Khuddus Anwar and Ors.
rules.reference: D.R. Gurushantappa v. Abdul Khuddus Anwar and Ors.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to hold that when a government undertaking is taken over by a separate corporate entity, employees become employees of the company and cease to be government servants.

rules.reference: U.P. State Roadways Organisation (Abolition of Posts and Absorption of Employees) Rules, 1982
rules.relevance: Defined the liability for pension and gratuity, stating the Government bears liability proportional to pre-deputation service, while the Corporation bears liability for family pension.

rules.reference: U.P. State Roadways Organisation (Abolition of Posts and Absorption of Employees) Rules, 1982
rules.relevance: Provided that failure to exercise the option under Rule 4 results in the employee being deemed to have opted for absorption in the Corporation.

rules.case_name: Som Prakash Rekhi v. Union of India & Another
rules.reference: Som Prakash Rekhi v. Union of India & Another
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this case because the petitioner in Som Prakash Rekhi had an existing right to pension under a voluntary retirement scheme when the Provident Fund Act became applicable. In the present case, the petitioners were temporary employees without such a right at the relevant time.

rules.reference: Government of India (Allocation of Business) Rules, 1961
rules.relevance: The court used these rules to determine that the Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT) does not have jurisdiction over Railway services, and thus DoPT circulars are not binding on the Railways.

rules.reference: Special Police Establishment (Executive Staff) Recruitment Rules, 1963
rules.relevance: The court examined these rules to establish that deputationists are not eligible for promotion in the regular quota and that posts held on deputation are treated as tenure posts.

rules.reference: Master Circular dated 29.01.1991
rules.relevance: The court relied on these clauses to establish that substitute teachers acquire temporary status after three months of continuous service, are screened by a Screening Committee, and are entitled to continuity of service from the date of acquiring temporary status upon regular absorption.

rules.reference: Conditions for extending benefit of concluded decision to non-parties
rules.relevance: The court laid down four specific circumstances under which the benefit of a concluded decision extends to those who did not approach the court: (a) representative capacity, (b) declaratory relief for a category, (c) quashing of general rules without restriction, or (d) express direction by the court. None applied here.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. N.R. Parmar
rules.reference: Union of India v. N.R. Parmar
rules.relevance: The court interpreted this precedent to clarify that seniority from the date of requisition applies only when the requisition year matches the vacancy year, and that the principle aims to remove arbitrariness caused by administrative delays.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: This rule empowers the court to hear a suit ex parte if the defendant does not appear when the suit is called on for hearing.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: The Explanation allows the court to proceed as if a party were present only if that specific party has already recorded evidence or a substantial portion thereof and then fails to appear.

rules.case_name: Rani Choudhury v. Lt.-Col. Suraj Jit Choudhury
rules.reference: Rani Choudhury v. Lt.-Col. Suraj Jit Choudhury
rules.relevance: Held that the Explanation to Order IX Rule 13 applies when an appeal is disposed of on any ground, including limitation, provided it is not withdrawn. The legislative intent is to confine the defendant to a single course of action.

rules.case_name: Messrs Mela Ram and Sons v. The Commissioner of Income Tax, Punjab
rules.reference: Messrs Mela Ram and Sons v. The Commissioner of Income Tax, Punjab
rules.relevance: Established that an appeal presented out of time is an appeal in the eye of law, and an order dismissing it as time-barred is a decision in the appeal.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: The Explanation bars an application to set aside an ex parte decree if an appeal against the decree has been disposed of on any ground other than withdrawal by the appellant.

rules.case_name: Shuja-Ud-Din v. The Union of India and Another
rules.reference: Shuja-Ud-Din v. The Union of India and Another
rules.relevance: Held that neither a Magistrate nor a Sessions Judge is competent to determine that an Indian national has acquired foreign nationality; only the Central Government can do so.

rules.reference: Adoption Regulations, 2017
rules.relevance: Provides that if one prospective adoptive parent is a foreigner and the other is an Indian, the case is treated at par with Indians living in India.

rules.case_name: Government of Andhra Pradesh v. Syed Mohd. Khan
rules.reference: Government of Andhra Pradesh v. Syed Mohd. Khan
rules.relevance: Held that the question of loss of Indian citizenship must be determined by the Central Government before a person can be treated as a foreigner.

rules.case_name: Izhar Ahmed Khan v. Union of India
rules.reference: Izhar Ahmed Khan v. Union of India
rules.relevance: The court relied on this decision for the principle that Parliament can regulate citizenship rights and that such provisions are not inconsistent with other Articles in Part II of the Constitution.

rules.case_name: Izhar Ahmad Khan v. Union of India
rules.reference: Izhar Ahmad Khan v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Upheld the legislative competence of Parliament to enact Section 9 of the Citizenship Act and the validity of Rule 3 of Schedule III to the Citizenship Rules.

rules.case_name: Mohd. Amim Vs. CBI
rules.reference: Mohd. Amim Vs. CBI
rules.relevance: Held that in conspiracy, it is not necessary for all conspirators to know every detail or participate from inception, provided there is unity of object.

rules.case_name: Anvar P. V. vs. P.K. Basheer and others
rules.reference: Anvar P. V. vs. P.K. Basheer and others
rules.relevance: Established that compliance with Section 65B is mandatory and inflexible for the admissibility of electronic records as secondary evidence.

rules.case_name: Mir Najaf Ali Askari vs. Central Bureau of Investigation
rules.reference: Mir Najaf Ali Askari vs. Central Bureau of Investigation
rules.relevance: Reinforced that conspiracy is hatched in secrecy and direct evidence is difficult to obtain, requiring inference from materials on record.

rules.case_name: Ferozuddin Basheeruddin and Others vs. State of Kerala
rules.reference: Ferozuddin Basheeruddin and Others vs. State of Kerala
rules.relevance: Established principles for proving criminal conspiracy, noting that it is a clandestine activity inferred from circumstantial evidence and that co-conspirators are liable for acts in furtherance of the common object.

rules.case_name: Bodhraj @ Bodham and Others vs. State of Jammu & Kashmir
rules.reference: Bodhraj @ Bodham and Others vs. State of Jammu & Kashmir
rules.relevance: Confirmed that information leading to discovery of facts is reliable and admissible under Section 27, regardless of whether it is confessional or non-inculpatory.

rules.case_name: Rajendra Pralhadrao Wasnik vs. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: Rajendra Pralhadrao Wasnik vs. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: Indicates that while Section 53A is not mandatory, failure to produce DNA evidence warrants an adverse inference.

rules.case_name: Krishan Kumar Malik vs. State of Haryana
rules.reference: Krishan Kumar Malik vs. State of Haryana
rules.relevance: Holds that failure to obtain forensic/DNA reports in rape cases is fatal to the prosecution's case.

rules.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
rules.relevance: Enables medical examination of accused in rape cases; failure to utilize this when reasonable grounds exist warrants adverse inference.

rules.case_name: Baldev Singh v. State of Haryana
rules.reference: Baldev Singh v. State of Haryana
rules.relevance: Relied upon for the tests governing cases based on circumstantial evidence, which the court found were satisfied in the present case.

rules.case_name: Ramnaresh v. State of Chhattisgarh
rules.reference: Ramnaresh v. State of Chhattisgarh
rules.relevance: Extensively quoted to restate the principles, aggravating circumstances, mitigating circumstances, and tests for imposing the death penalty.

rules.reference: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
rules.relevance: Circumscribes the jurisdiction of the NCLAT to matters other than the commercial wisdom of dissenting financial creditors.

rules.reference: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons) Regulations, 2016
rules.relevance: The court analyzed the applicability of the unamended regulation in force at the time of the advertisement to determine if the process was vitiated.

rules.reference: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
rules.relevance: Defines the limited grounds on which the NCLT can examine an approved resolution plan, excluding scrutiny of commercial wisdom.

rules.reference: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
rules.relevance: Empowers the NCLT to entertain any question of law or fact arising out of insolvency proceedings, supporting the exercise of inherent powers.

rules.case_name: K. Sashidhar vs. Indian Overseas Bank
rules.reference: K. Sashidhar vs. Indian Overseas Bank
rules.relevance: Established that the commercial wisdom of the Committee of Creditors is non-justiciable and cannot be challenged before the adjudicating authority or appellate tribunal.

rules.case_name: Bishnu Biswas v. Union of India
rules.reference: Bishnu Biswas v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Distinguished because the respondent did not challenge the inclusion of the interview/experience component as a new rule, but contested the merit comparison.

rules.case_name: C.P. Kalra Vs Air India
rules.reference: C.P. Kalra Vs Air India
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this case, noting it was prior to the All India Judges' Association judgment and that the specific recruitment rules here mandate merit-cum-seniority.

rules.provision: Schedule 'B', General Instructions and Grading Table
rules.reference: Manipur Judicial Service Rules, 2005
rules.relevance: The majority noted that the grading table assigns Grade 'F' (Value 0) to scores below 40%, implying that 40% is the implicit threshold for a passing grade, justifying the cut-off.

rules.case_name: All India Judges’ Association and Ors. Vs. Union of India and Ors.
rules.reference: All India Judges’ Association and Ors. Vs. Union of India and Ors.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment which directed that recruitment to Higher Judicial Services must be based on 'merit-cum-seniority' and a suitability test, forming the basis for the impugned rules.

rules.reference: Gujarat State Judicial Service Rules, 2005
rules.relevance: The court examined whether the High Court's selection method complied with Rule 5(1)(i), which mandates promotion based on 'merit-cum-seniority' and a suitability test.

rules.reference: Participation and Challenge
rules.relevance: While candidates who participate in a selection process generally cannot challenge the procedure, this does not bar challenges to the inclusion of ineligible candidates where the process itself is arbitrary or illegal.

rules.case_name: Chairman and Managing Director, Food Corporation of India and Others Vs. Jagdish Balaram Bahira and Others
rules.reference: Chairman and Managing Director, Food Corporation of India and Others Vs. Jagdish Balaram Bahira and Others
rules.relevance: Held that selection of ineligible persons is a systemic failure that violates the rights of eligible persons and good governance.

rules.reference: Self-Certification Limitations
rules.relevance: Self-attestation of documents is procedural; it does not constitute a substantive declaration of equivalence between different qualifications.

rules.reference: Representative Impleadment
rules.relevance: In cases challenging the legality of a select list based on eligibility criteria, impleading every selected candidate is not necessary if representative parties are present.

rules.reference: Duty of Recruiting Agency
rules.relevance: The recruiting agency has an obligation to scrutinize qualifications and cannot abdicate this duty by relying solely on self-certification by candidates for equivalence.

rules.case_name: Shri Sitaram Sugar Company & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.reference: Shri Sitaram Sugar Company & Anr. v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.relevance: Establishes that judicial review is not concerned with matters of economic policy and courts should not substitute their judgment for that of expert regulatory bodies.

rules.reference: Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act, 2008
rules.relevance: Mandates that AERA consider concessions offered by the Central Government in agreements like the OMDA and SSA when determining tariffs.

rules.reference: Airports Economic Regulatory Authority of India Act, 2008
rules.relevance: Defines 'aeronautical service' to include services for supplying fuel to aircraft, supporting the classification of FTC as aeronautical.

rules.reference: State Support Agreement (SSA)
rules.relevance: Stipulates that the Annual Fee shall not be included as part of costs for provision of Aeronautical Services and no pass-through is available.

rules.reference: Operation, Management and Development Agreement (OMDA)
rules.relevance: Lists 'common hydrant infrastructure for aircraft fuelling services' as an aeronautical service.

rules.reference: Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
rules.relevance: Defines the offence of intentionally insulting or intimidating with intent to humiliate a member of a Scheduled Caste or Scheduled Tribe in any place within public view.

rules.case_name: Khuman Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.reference: Khuman Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.relevance: Held that the victim's caste alone is insufficient to attract the Act; the offence must be committed on the ground that the victim belongs to a Scheduled Caste.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.
rules.reference: Union of India v. State of Maharashtra & Ors.
rules.relevance: Confirmed that proceedings under Section 482 CrPC can be invoked if an FIR is found to be false or unsubstantiated.

rules.reference: The Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
