rules.reference: Shatrughna Baban Meshram Vs. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: Guided the court in commuting the death sentence to life imprisonment, considering the specific circumstances and the availability of a wider spectrum of punishment under Section 376A IPC.

rules.case_name: Mohan Singh vs. Prem Singh & Anr.
rules.reference: Mohan Singh vs. Prem Singh & Anr.
rules.relevance: Held that the inculpatory part of a statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C. can be used to lend credence to prosecution evidence if the exculpatory part is false.

rules.reference: Crime and Criminal Test
rules.relevance: The requirement to examine both the nature of the crime (aggravating circumstances) and the criminal (mitigating circumstances) before awarding death.

rules.case_name: Shatrughna Baban Meshram v. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: Shatrughna Baban Meshram v. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: Held that the theory of 'residual doubt' has no place in Indian jurisprudence for sentencing in circumstantial evidence cases.

rules.case_name: Vinay Balachandra Joshi v. Registrar General, Supreme Court of India
rules.reference: Vinay Balachandra Joshi v. Registrar General, Supreme Court of India
rules.relevance: Established that there is no fundamental right to be allotted a chamber; it is a facility provided by the Court subject to reasonable rules.

rules.reference: Proximity of Block Period
rules.relevance: The court established that the block period for eligibility must be proximate to the application date to ensure the advocate is in active practice.

rules.reference: SCAORA Rules and Regulations
rules.relevance: This rule requires SCBA membership for SCAORA membership, rendering the challenge to SCBA exclusivity academic.

rules.reference: Supreme Court Lawyers’ Chambers (Allotment and Occupancy) Rules
rules.relevance: This rule mandates SCBA membership for allotment; the court upheld its validity.

rules.case_name: Vinay Balchandra Joshi Vs. Registrar General of Supreme Court of India
rules.reference: Vinay Balchandra Joshi Vs. Registrar General of Supreme Court of India
rules.relevance: The criteria adopted in this case for allotment of Chambers were relied upon by the Court to identify advocates who practised regularly in the Supreme Court for voting eligibility.

rules.reference: Consolidation of Proceedings
rules.relevance: The court applied the principle that peripheral proceedings arising from interim orders should not proceed independently if the main dispute is pending adjudication in a competent forum, to avoid multiplicity of proceedings.

rules.reference: Scope of remand and appellate review
rules.relevance: When a higher court sets aside only a specific finding (such as maintainability) and remands the case, the lower court is expected to decide the remaining substantive issues based on the existing record, rather than remanding the entire matter for fresh adjudication unless necessary.

rules.case_name: Ghanashyam Mishra & Sons Private Limited v. Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company Limited
rules.citation: M.A. No. 1166 of 2021 in CA No. 8129 of 2019
rules.reference: Ghanashyam Mishra & Sons Private Limited v. Edelweiss Asset Reconstruction Company Limited
rules.relevance: Held that filing miscellaneous applications to seek review or modification of orders is an abuse of the process of law.

rules.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure
rules.relevance: The provisions under which the additional application sought initiation of proceedings.

rules.case_name: Vimlesh Kumari Kulshrestha vs. Sambhajirao and another
rules.reference: Vimlesh Kumari Kulshrestha vs. Sambhajirao and another
rules.relevance: Cited by the High Court regarding the requirement of court liberty when withdrawing a suit to file a fresh one on the same cause of action.

rules.reference: Assessment of delay in disciplinary proceedings
rules.relevance: The court established that delay must be assessed on facts, specifically looking for condonation of lapses by the employer or prejudice to the employee. No hard-and-fast rule exists for quashing proceedings solely on delay.

rules.case_name: Government of Andhra Pradesh and Others vs. V. Appala Swamy
rules.reference: Government of Andhra Pradesh and Others vs. V. Appala Swamy
rules.relevance: Relied upon for the specific principles that proceedings can be quashed for delay only if the employer condoned lapses or if prejudice was caused to the employee.

rules.case_name: Arjun Chaubey v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.reference: Arjun Chaubey v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.relevance: Held that an order of dismissal passed by a disciplinary authority against an employee for misconduct concerning the authority himself is vitiated due to violation of natural justice, and such grave illegality cannot be cured by the employee's past misconduct.

rules.case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Bani Singh and Another
rules.reference: State of Madhya Pradesh vs. Bani Singh and Another
rules.relevance: Cited to distinguish cases involving unexplained delay in the initiation of proceedings from the present case where the delay occurred after a remand.

rules.case_name: M. V Bijlani vs. Union of India
rules.reference: M. V Bijlani vs. Union of India
rules.relevance: Held that an Enquiry Officer cannot reject relevant testimony on surmises and must base conclusions on preponderance of probability.

rules.case_name: P. Purushottam Reddy and another vs. Pratap Steels Ltd
rules.reference: P. Purushottam Reddy and another vs. Pratap Steels Ltd
rules.relevance: Establishes that remand is not justified when the trial court has recorded findings on all issues and no additional evidence is required, particularly when the issue was not pleaded in the written statement.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: The court held that a decree on default under this rule was unsustainable because the trial court never formally treated the amended written statement as a counter-claim or directed the other parties to file an answer.

rules.case_name: Ramesh Chand Ardawatiya v. Anil Panjwani
rules.reference: Ramesh Chand Ardawatiya v. Anil Panjwani
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this precedent, noting it did not address whether a counter-claim can be filed after trial conclusion or solely against a co-defendant.

rules.reference: Finality of dismissed suit
rules.relevance: The court held that since the plaintiff's suit was dismissed and not appealed, the dismissal became final, and the High Court erred in remanding the suit.

rules.reference: Counter-claim must be directed against the plaintiff
rules.relevance: The court established that a counter-claim directed solely against co-defendants, without any claim against the plaintiff, cannot be maintained and cannot convert litigation into an inter-pleader suit.

rules.reference: Specific Relief Act, 1963
rules.relevance: This provision allows a court to direct specific performance of the performable part of a contract if the plaintiff pays the full consideration and relinquishes claims to the unperformable part and compensation. The court analyzed whether this relief must be pleaded in the initial plaint or can be sought via amendment at the appellate stage.

rules.case_name: A.L. Parthasarathi Mudaliar v. Vertkata Kondiah Chettiar
rules.reference: A.L. Parthasarathi Mudaliar v. Vertkata Kondiah Chettiar
rules.relevance: The court relied on this decision to support the proposition that a plaintiff can relinquish part of the performance of a contract at the appellate stage if the defaulting party is incapable of performing the whole.

rules.case_name: Kalyanpur Lime Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar
rules.reference: Kalyanpur Lime Works Ltd. v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to establish that relief based on the Specific Relief Act can be granted at any stage of litigation.

rules.reference: An appeal is a continuation of the suit
rules.relevance: The court applied this principle to hold that the appellate court can consider questions relating to the rights of parties, including amendments to pleadings, provided the right existed at the time of filing the suit.

rules.reference: Specific Relief Act
rules.relevance: Governs specific performance of part of a contract where the unperformed part does not admit of compensation in money. Requires the party seeking performance to pay the full consideration without abatement and relinquish all claims to the remaining part of the contract.

rules.reference: Circumstantial Evidence and Unexplained Circumstances
rules.relevance: Failure to explain incriminating circumstances or offering a false explanation serves as an additional link in the chain of circumstantial evidence.

rules.case_name: Neel Kumar@ Anil Kumar v. State of Haryana
rules.reference: Neel Kumar@ Anil Kumar v. State of Haryana
rules.relevance: Observed that keeping silent or failing to explain incriminating circumstances under Section 313 CrPC is an additional link in the chain of circumstances.

rules.case_name: Eswarappa alias Doopada Eswarappa v. State of Karnataka
rules.reference: Eswarappa alias Doopada Eswarappa v. State of Karnataka
rules.relevance: Relied on regarding medical jurisprudence, specifically that absence of marks of violence or struggle suggests suicide rather than homicidal hanging.

rules.case_name: Subramaniam v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: Subramaniam v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.relevance: Held that the circumstance of husband and wife living together does not conclusively prove guilt in the absence of evidence of violence.

rules.case_name: Ponnusamy v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: Ponnusamy v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.relevance: Establishes that the absence of a hyoid bone fracture does not exclude strangulation as a cause of death, as fractures are age-dependent and not present in all cases.

rules.reference: Finance Act, 1994
rules.relevance: Establishes the levy of service tax on taxable services, subject to exemptions.

rules.case_name: Association of Leasing & Financial Service Companies v. Union of India
rules.reference: Association of Leasing & Financial Service Companies v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Relied upon for the principle that service tax is a value-added tax and imposed every time a service is rendered.

rules.case_name: Commissioner of Central Excise, Aurangabad v. Bajaj Auto Ltd.
rules.reference: Commissioner of Central Excise, Aurangabad v. Bajaj Auto Ltd.
rules.relevance: Relied upon for the principles governing wilful suppression and the invocation of the extended period of limitation.

rules.case_name: Ferro Alloys Corpn. Ltd. v. A.P. State Electricity Board
rules.reference: Ferro Alloys Corpn. Ltd. v. A.P. State Electricity Board
rules.relevance: Relied upon to define 'interest' and distinguish it from consideration for services, rejecting the argument that interchange fee is interest.

rules.reference: Finance Act, 1994
rules.relevance: Defines 'credit card, debit card, charge card or other payment card service' to include services provided by any person, including an issuing bank and an acquiring bank, in relation to the settlement of any amount transacted through such card.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The court cited this section regarding punishment for non-attendance in obedience to an order from a public servant to highlight the legal consequences of the appellants' conduct.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The court cited this section regarding punishment for non-appearance in response to a proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C.

rules.case_name: Siddharth v. State of Uttar Pradesh
rules.reference: Siddharth v. State of Uttar Pradesh
rules.relevance: Highlighted the distinction between the existence of the power to arrest and the justification for exercising it, stressing personal liberty.

rules.case_name: Prem Shankar Prasad v. State of Bihar and Anr.
rules.reference: Prem Shankar Prasad v. State of Bihar and Anr.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this decision to affirm that an accused who is absconding and against whom proceedings under Sections 82/83 Cr.P.C. are initiated is not entitled to anticipatory bail.

rules.case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Pradeep Sharma
rules.reference: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Pradeep Sharma
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to establish that a person declared as an absconder/proclaimed offender under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is not entitled to anticipatory bail.

rules.reference: Industrial Disputes Act, 1947
rules.relevance: Provides that an application for closure is deemed allowed if not decided within 60 days; used to assess the bona fides of the company's withdrawal.

rules.case_name: Workmen of the Straw Board Manufacturing Company Limited v. M/s. Straw Board Manufacturing Company Limited
rules.reference: Workmen of the Straw Board Manufacturing Company Limited v. M/s. Straw Board Manufacturing Company Limited
rules.relevance: Emphasized functional integrality in determining if units constitute one establishment for closure purposes.

rules.case_name: Management of Hindustan Steel Limited v. The Workmen
rules.reference: Management of Hindustan Steel Limited v. The Workmen
rules.relevance: Defined 'undertaking' in its ordinary sense, allowing parts of a business to be treated as undertakings.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Recognition of Trade Unions and Prevention of Unfair Labour Practices Act, 1971
rules.relevance: Defines 'Failure to implement award, settlement or agreement' as an unfair labour practice.

rules.case_name: Sarguja Transport Service v. State Transport Appellate Tribunal, Gwalior and Ors.
rules.reference: Sarguja Transport Service v. State Transport Appellate Tribunal, Gwalior and Ors.
rules.relevance: Established that a writ petition withdrawn without liberty to refile cannot be refiled to prevent bench-hunting; distinguished here as the withdrawal was bona fide for settlement.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. S.L. Verma
rules.reference: Union of India v. S.L. Verma
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to hold that once the deeming provision applies, subsequent options to remain in CPF are invalid, and employees become members of the Pension Scheme by operation of law.

rules.reference: Office Memorandum dated 01.05.1987
rules.relevance: The court interpreted the OM to establish a legal fiction deeming employees to have switched to the Pension Scheme unless they explicitly opted out by the cut-off date.

rules.case_name: Ramrao v. All India Backward Class Bank Employees Welfare Assn.
rules.reference: Ramrao v. All India Backward Class Bank Employees Welfare Assn.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to hold that fixing a cut-off date for promotions or benefits does not offend Article 14.

rules.reference: Banking Companies (Acquisition and Transfer of Undertaking) Act, 1970
rules.relevance: The court considered whether the regulations were beyond the scope of this section, which protects existing pensionary rights, concluding the appellant could not invoke it as he was not an officer when the regulations were introduced.

rules.case_name: Krishena Kumar & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.reference: Krishena Kumar & Ors. v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this decision to establish that pension and provident fund schemes are structurally different, and CPF retirees do not have a continuing obligation or right to switch to a pension scheme.

rules.reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
rules.relevance: Mandates that the arbitral tribunal shall decide in accordance with the terms of the contract.

rules.reference: Patent Illegality
rules.relevance: The court established that an award can be set aside if it is patently illegal, i.e., in contravention of the Act, substantive law, or terms of the contract.

rules.case_name: Renusagar Power Co. Ltd. v. General Electric Co.
rules.reference: Renusagar Power Co. Ltd. v. General Electric Co.
rules.relevance: Defined 'public policy' narrowly for foreign awards; the court distinguished this to apply a wider meaning to domestic awards under Section 34.

rules.case_name: Fateh Chand v. Balkishan Das
rules.reference: Fateh Chand v. Balkishan Das
rules.relevance: Established that under Section 74, if a sum is a genuine pre-estimate of damages, the party is entitled to reasonable compensation without proving actual loss.

rules.case_name: Maula Bux v. Union of India
rules.reference: Maula Bux v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Clarified that while proof of loss is not always required, genuine pre-estimates are valid measures of compensation unless challenged as penalties.

rules.case_name: Geeta Mehrotra and another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another
rules.reference: Geeta Mehrotra and another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another
rules.relevance: Distinguished on facts: involved brother and sister of husband after divorce, whereas present case involves husband and parents during subsistence of marriage.

rules.case_name: Neechu Chopra and another vs. Bharti
rules.reference: Neechu Chopra and another vs. Bharti
rules.relevance: Distinguished on facts: in that case, the husband had died and parents were too old, whereas here the accused are the husband and parents actively alleged to have harassed the wife.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The specific charge of rape under which the FIR was registered.

rules.case_name: Naim Ahamed v. State (NCT of Delhi)
rules.reference: Naim Ahamed v. State (NCT of Delhi)
rules.relevance: Established that a mature, married woman who has consensual relations for years cannot claim rape based on a false promise to marry, as her consent is not vitiated by misconception of fact.

rules.case_name: Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and Anr
rules.reference: Amit Kapoor vs. Ramesh Chander and Anr
rules.relevance: Establishes principles for quashing: power must be exercised sparingly; court should not examine evidence reliability at threshold; quashing is permissible only if allegations are patently absurd or do not prima facie establish an offense.

rules.reference: Appointment Rules, 2012
rules.relevance: The respondents submitted that the advertisements were issued in accordance with these rules, establishing the procedural validity of the selection process.

rules.case_name: Dr. Krushna Chandra Sahu and Others v. State of Orissa and Others
rules.reference: Dr. Krushna Chandra Sahu and Others v. State of Orissa and Others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to hold that Selection Committees do not have the jurisdiction to lay down criteria for selection unless specifically authorized by rules.

rules.case_name: Hari Sharma and Ors. Vs. State of Jharkhand
rules.citation: Writ Petition No.1130 of 2017 (Jharkhand High Court)
rules.reference: Hari Sharma and Ors. Vs. State of Jharkhand
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this decision because it was stayed by the Division Bench and pending appeal, and the controversy regarding the combination post was different from the specific issue in the present case.

rules.case_name: Bedanga Talukdar v. Saifudaullah Khan and Others
rules.reference: Bedanga Talukdar v. Saifudaullah Khan and Others
rules.relevance: The court used this case to establish that any power of relaxation of selection procedure must be mentioned in the advertisement to ensure equal opportunity.

rules.case_name: N.T. Devin Katti and Others v. Karnataka Public Service Commission and Others
rules.reference: N.T. Devin Katti and Others v. Karnataka Public Service Commission and Others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to clarify that while candidates do not have a vested right to selection, they have a vested right to be considered in accordance with the rules existing on the date of the advertisement.

rules.reference: State Bank of India Officers' Service Rules, 1992 (SBIOSR)
rules.relevance: Allows continuation of disciplinary proceedings after superannuation if initiated before cessation of service. The court held this rule inapplicable as proceedings had already concluded.

rules.case_name: State Bank of India & Ors. v. Kamal Kishore Prasad
rules.citation: Order dated 25.11.2013 in SLP (C) No. 16541 of 2010
rules.reference: State Bank of India & Ors. v. Kamal Kishore Prasad
rules.relevance: The Supreme Court's earlier order in the same matter directed the Appointing Authority to take an appropriate decision keeping all contentions open, which formed the basis for the fresh proceedings.

rules.reference: State Bank of India Officers' Service Rules, 1992 (SBIOSR)
rules.relevance: Defines the age of superannuation and the discretion to extend service. The court analyzed this to determine the respondent's service status.

rules.reference: UCO Bank Officer Employees' Services Regulations, 1979
rules.relevance: This regulation creates a legal fiction that an officer ceases to be in service on superannuation but proceedings continue 'as if' he was in service. The court analyzed whether this applies when proceedings are initiated post-retirement.

rules.reference: Loss of confidence as a factor in determining punishment
rules.relevance: Loss of confidence in an employee due to gross negligence or breach of banking procedures is a relevant factor in imposing termination, even in the absence of dishonest intent or misappropriation.

rules.reference: FIR Content Requirements
rules.relevance: An FIR need not contain every minute detail or specific overt acts of each accused; it must only reveal the broad picture and essential details.

rules.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure
rules.relevance: Governs police inquest. The court held that the scope is limited to ascertaining the apparent cause of death and does not require recording detailed overt acts of accused.

rules.reference: Identification of Dead Body
rules.relevance: Identification can be established through visible features, photographs, and personal effects (like a belt) even if the body is bloated.

rules.case_name: Shere v. State of U.P.
rules.reference: Shere v. State of U.P.
rules.relevance: Held that in cases with large numbers of accused, conviction should be limited to those with clearly established presence and overt acts.

rules.case_name: Babu v. State of Kerala
rules.reference: Standard for Appellate Interference with Acquittal
rules.relevance: The court applied the principle that appellate courts should only interfere with acquittals if the findings are perverse, based on erroneous law, or lead to a miscarriage of justice.

rules.reference: Work Charged Establishment Revised Service Conditions (Repealing) Rules, 2013
rules.relevance: The court upheld this rule, which mandates counting one year of regular service for every five years of work-charged service for pension calculation, and using work-charged service only to make up shortfalls in qualifying service.

rules.reference: Distinction between regular and work-charged employees
rules.relevance: The court relied on the principle that work-charged employees are not appointed on substantive posts and thus their service cannot be fully counted for pension quantum, only for qualifying service.

rules.case_name: Prem Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Ors.
rules.reference: Prem Singh Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Ors.
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this precedent, holding that it only required work-charged service to be counted for qualifying service for pension, not for determining the quantum of pension.

rules.reference: Railway Services (Pension) Rules, 1993
rules.relevance: The court considered the respondent's argument that this rule treats contractual service followed by appointment to a substantive post as permanent service for pension calculation.

rules.case_name: Dhyan Singh & Ors. v. State of Haryana & Ors.
rules.reference: Dhyan Singh & Ors. v. State of Haryana & Ors.
rules.relevance: Held that service under a specific scheme funded by the Central Government cannot be counted for pensionary benefits or salary fixation upon regular absorption.

rules.case_name: A. Srinivasulu v. State Rep. by the Inspector of Police
rules.reference: A. Srinivasulu v. State Rep. by the Inspector of Police
rules.relevance: Distinguished on facts; involved criminal conspiracy where co-conspirators were protected, whereas the present case involves direct fabrication of documents which is not a protected official act.

rules.case_name: D. Devaraja v. Obais Sanders Hussain
rules.reference: D. Devaraja v. Obais Sanders Hussain
rules.relevance: Reaffirmed that Section 197 does not extend to every act done by a public servant while in service, but only those in discharge of official duty.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code
rules.relevance: The court considered the serious nature of these offences (criminal breach of trust, cheating, forgery) to determine whether the High Court had adequately assessed the gravity of the allegations before granting interim protection.

rules.reference: U.P. Societies Registration Act, 1860
rules.relevance: Empowers the Assistant Registrar to cancel the registration of proceedings related to amendments if they are found to be contrary to the Act or Rules.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: These sections defined the offences of cheating, forgery, and using forged documents alleged against the appellant, forming the basis for the criminal complaint.

rules.case_name: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Boghara Polyfab (P) Ltd.
rules.reference: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Boghara Polyfab (P) Ltd.
rules.relevance: Categorized issues in Section 11 applications, holding that the existence of an arbitration agreement is a mandatory issue for the court to decide, particularly when forgery is alleged.

rules.reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
rules.relevance: Defines the power of the Chief Justice or his designate to appoint an arbitrator and the scope of preliminary issues to be decided at this stage.

rules.case_name: Bharat Rasiklal Ashra vs. Gautam Rasiklal Ashra & Anr.
rules.reference: Bharat Rasiklal Ashra vs. Gautam Rasiklal Ashra & Anr.
rules.relevance: Reiterated that the question of whether there is an arbitration agreement is a jurisdictional issue to be decided by the Chief Justice/designate, not the arbitrator.

rules.case_name: SBP & Co. vs. Patel Engg. Ltd.
rules.reference: SBP & Co. vs. Patel Engg. Ltd.
rules.relevance: Established that the Chief Justice or his designate must decide whether an arbitration agreement exists before appointing an arbitrator.

rules.case_name: Nathani Steels Ltd. v. Associated Constructions
rules.reference: Nathani Steels Ltd. v. Associated Constructions
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this case, holding that it did not apply because there was no full and final settlement in the present facts, unlike in Nathani Steels.

rules.case_name: Thamma Venkata Subbamma (dead) by Lrs. V Thamma Rattamma and Others
rules.reference: Thamma Venkata Subbamma (dead) by Lrs. V Thamma Rattamma and Others
rules.relevance: Establishes that a gift by a coparcener of his undivided interest in coparcenary property is void ab initio.

rules.reference: Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956
rules.relevance: The court interpreted the phrase 'unless and until it is disproved' to establish that the presumption regarding registered adoption documents is rebuttable, not irrebuttable.

rules.reference: Hindu Adoption and Maintenance Act, 1956
rules.relevance: The court applied the requirement that a child must be actually given and taken in adoption with intent to transfer from the family of birth to the family of adoption, identifying this as a sine qua non for validity.

rules.reference: Scope of appellate interference
rules.relevance: The court held that superior courts can only interfere with factual findings in very exceptional cases involving extreme perversity, and cannot re-appreciate evidence routinely.

rules.case_name: Madan Singh v. Mst. Sham Kaur and Ors.
rules.reference: Madan Singh v. Mst. Sham Kaur and Ors.
rules.relevance: The court concurred with the observations in this case regarding the nature of the presumption under Section 16.

rules.case_name: Prahlad Singh Bhati v. NCT, Delhi and Another
rules.reference: Prahlad Singh Bhati v. NCT, Delhi and Another
rules.relevance: Cited for factors to consider in bail, including nature of accusations, severity of punishment, and apprehension of witness tampering.

rules.case_name: Ram Govind Upadhyay v. Sudarshan Singh and Others
rules.reference: Ram Govind Upadhyay v. Sudarshan Singh and Others
rules.relevance: Establishes that bail discretion must be exercised judiciously, considering the heinous nature of the crime, severity of punishment, and prima facie evidence.

rules.reference: Balance between Liberty and Social Security
rules.relevance: Individual liberty is not absolute and must be balanced against collective security and the rule of law, especially in cases involving heinous crimes.

rules.case_name: Dr. Narendra K. Amin v. State of Gujarat and another
rules.reference: Dr. Narendra K. Amin v. State of Gujarat and another
rules.relevance: Holds that an order granting bail is vulnerable if irrelevant materials are considered or relevant factors are ignored, rendering it perverse.

rules.case_name: Prasanta Kumar Sarkar v. Ashis Chatterjee and another
rules.reference: Prasanta Kumar Sarkar v. Ashis Chatterjee and another
rules.relevance: Lists factors for bail consideration including prima facie grounds, gravity of accusation, danger of absconding, and character of the accused.

rules.case_name: CBI v. Thommandru Hannah Vijayalakshmi
rules.reference: CBI v. Thommandru Hannah Vijayalakshmi
rules.relevance: Held that Income Tax Returns are not conclusive proof of lawful sources of income in PC Act cases and that the Investigating Officer is not required to consider the accused's explanation before filing a chargesheet.

rules.case_name: Nanjappa Vs. State of Karnataka
rules.reference: Nanjappa Vs. State of Karnataka
rules.relevance: Clarifies that Section 19(3) bars appellate/revisional interference but does not prevent the Special Judge from discharging an accused if sanction is invalid; emphasizes that objections should be raised at the earliest stage.

rules.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
rules.relevance: Contemplates the transfer of cases to higher courts, including the High Court itself, establishing that such transfers are part of the 'procedure established by law' and do not inherently violate Article 21.

rules.case_name: Sajjan Kumar v. CBI
rules.reference: Sajjan Kumar v. CBI
rules.relevance: Establishes the principles for framing charges under Sections 227/228 (applicable to 238/239), stating that if materials disclose grave suspicion against the accused which has not been properly explained, the court is justified in framing charges.

rules.case_name: K. Chandrasekhar v. State of Kerala and Others
rules.reference: K. Chandrasekhar v. State of Kerala and Others
rules.relevance: Relied upon to distinguish between 'further investigation' (continuation) and 'reinvestigation' (fresh start), holding only the former is permissible under Section 173(8).

rules.reference: Assessment of flight risk
rules.relevance: The status of the accused, such as being a sitting MLA, is relevant in assessing the remoteness of the possibility of absconsion.

rules.case_name: Daulat Ram and others v. State of Haryana
rules.reference: Daulat Ram and others v. State of Haryana
rules.relevance: Holds that cancellation of bail requires cogent and overwhelming circumstances or supervening events non-conducive to a fair trial.

rules.case_name: Vipin Kumar Dhir v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Vipin Kumar Dhir v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: Holds that bail can be revoked if the court considered irrelevant factors or ignored relevant material, rendering the order legally untenable.

rules.reference: Effect of charge-sheet on bail considerations
rules.relevance: Once a charge-sheet is filed, the risk of tampering with evidence or interfering with the investigation is generally considered no longer relevant.

rules.case_name: Kalyan Chandra Sarkar v. Rajesh Ranjan @ Pappu Yadav and another
rules.reference: Kalyan Chandra Sarkar v. Rajesh Ranjan @ Pappu Yadav and another
rules.relevance: Establishes parameters for granting bail, including nature of accusation, severity of punishment, and apprehension of witness tampering.

rules.case_name: A. Srinivasulu v. State Rep. by the Inspector of Police
rules.reference: A. Srinivasulu v. State Rep. by the Inspector of Police
rules.relevance: Distinguished on facts; involved criminal conspiracy where co-conspirators were protected, whereas the present case involves direct fabrication of documents which is not a protected official act.

rules.case_name: Harihar Prasad v. State of Bihar
rules.reference: Harihar Prasad v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: Held that offences of criminal conspiracy (Section 120-B IPC) and criminal misconduct (Section 5(2) P.C. Act) are not part of a public servant's official duty, so Section 197 CrPC sanction is not a bar to prosecution.

rules.case_name: D. Devaraja v. Obais Sanders Hussain
rules.reference: D. Devaraja v. Obais Sanders Hussain
rules.relevance: Reaffirmed that Section 197 does not extend to every act done by a public servant while in service, but only those in discharge of official duty.

rules.case_name: Lalu Prasad alias Lalu Prasad Yadav v. State of Bihar
rules.reference: Lalu Prasad alias Lalu Prasad Yadav v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: The court cited this case to establish that Section 197 CrPC and Section 19 PC Act operate in conceptually different fields.

rules.case_name: S.K. Miglani v. State (NCT of Delhi)
rules.reference: S.K. Miglani v. State (NCT of Delhi)
rules.relevance: The court relied on this case to affirm that a bank manager cannot claim protection under Section 197 CrPC as they are not removable only with government sanction.

rules.reference: Discovery of Facts at Instance of Accused
rules.relevance: Recovery of the body and incriminating articles at the instance of the accused serves as strong corroborative evidence of guilt.

rules.reference: Failure to cross-examine on material issues
rules.relevance: The court held that if a question is not put to a witness in cross-examination who could furnish an explanation, the correctness or legality of that fact/issue cannot be raised later.

rules.case_name: A Shanker v. State of Karnataka
rules.reference: A Shanker v. State of Karnataka
rules.relevance: Cited to support the principle that normal discrepancies due to errors of observation or memory do not render evidence unreliable if they do not affect the core of the case.

rules.reference: Minor discrepancies in witness testimony
rules.relevance: The court held that minor contradictions or embellishments on trivial matters do not affect the core of the prosecution case and should not lead to rejection of evidence.

rules.reference: Limitations of 'last seen' theory
rules.relevance: The court held that the circumstance of being last seen together does not by itself lead to an inference of guilt; there must be additional evidence establishing connectivity between the accused and the crime.

rules.case_name: Narcotics Control Bureau v. Karma Phuntsok and Ors.
rules.reference: Narcotics Control Bureau v. Karma Phuntsok and Ors.
rules.relevance: Rejected the argument that Section 37 does not apply if the Public Prosecutor does not explicitly oppose bail, holding that the appearance of the Prosecutor suggests opposition and the statutory conditions must still be met.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. Gurcharan Singh
rules.reference: Union of India v. Gurcharan Singh
rules.relevance: Established that the High Court must bear in mind the provisions of Section 37 of the NDPS Act before releasing an accused on bail.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. Abdulla
rules.reference: Union of India v. Abdulla
rules.relevance: Emphasized that it is mandatory for the court to hear the Public Prosecutor and come to a prima facie conclusion that there is no material to convict the accused before granting bail.

rules.case_name: Collector of Customs, New Delhi v. Ahmadalieva Nodira
rules.reference: Collector of Customs, New Delhi v. Ahmadalieva Nodira
rules.relevance: Clarified that the twin conditions under Section 37(1)(b) are cumulative and that 'reasonable grounds' requires substantial probable causes for believing the accused is not guilty, which is a higher standard than prima facie grounds.

rules.case_name: Birakishore Ktfr v. State of Orissa
rules.reference: Birakishore Ktfr v. State of Orissa
rules.relevance: Held that recovery from a plastic bag belonging to the accused does not attract Section 50.

rules.case_name: Ibrahim Nazeer v. State of Tamil Nadu and Anr.
rules.reference: Ibrahim Nazeer v. State of Tamil Nadu and Anr.
rules.relevance: Cited to support the High Court's rejection of the appellant's stand regarding the likelihood of bail.

rules.reference: Impact of act determines relatability to public order
rules.relevance: The court relied on the principle that the intensity and impact of acts on the moral fibre of the community determine if they affect public order, rather than just the number of acts.

rules.case_name: Senthamilselvi v. State of TN. and Anr.
rules.reference: Senthamilselvi v. State of TN. and Anr.
rules.relevance: Cited to support the High Court's rejection of the appellant's stand regarding the likelihood of bail.

rules.reference: Subjective satisfaction of detaining authority regarding likelihood of bail
rules.relevance: The court held that the detaining authority's satisfaction regarding the likelihood of release on bail, based on materials, is not to be interfered with unless it is ipse-dixit.

rules.reference: Tamil Nadu Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Drug Offenders, Forest Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Slum Grabbers and Video Pirates Act, 1982
rules.relevance: The statutory provision under which the detenu was detained as an 'immoral traffic offender'.

rules.case_name: Sohan Lal Passi vs. P. Sesh Reddy and others
rules.reference: Sohan Lal Passi vs. P. Sesh Reddy and others
rules.relevance: Affirmed that the insurance company must establish that the insured was guilty of a wilful infringement of the promise. If the insured appointed a duly licensed driver and the accident occurred due to unauthorized use, the insurer cannot repudiate liability without proof of the insured's fault.

rules.case_name: Ram Chandra Singh vs. Rajaram and others
rules.reference: Ram Chandra Singh vs. Rajaram and others
rules.relevance: Clarified that an insurer is absolved of liability only if the owner was aware the licence was fake but still permitted the driver to drive. The mere fact of a fake licence does not absolve the insurer.

rules.case_name: Skandia Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Kokilaben Chandravadan and others
rules.reference: Skandia Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Kokilaben Chandravadan and others
rules.relevance: Established that 'breach' implies a wilful infringement or violation by the insured. The insurer must prove the insured was at fault and guilty of violating the promise to employ a duly licensed driver.

rules.reference: Burden of Proof and Due Diligence
rules.relevance: The insurer bears the burden to prove by cogent evidence that the insured committed a willful breach or failed to exercise reasonable care. There is no statutory or policy mandate requiring owners to verify licences with the RTO unless the licence is demonstrably fake on its face or expired.

rules.reference: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
rules.relevance: The court used these provisions to determine that while the insurer must pay third-party claims, it is entitled to recover the amount from the insured if there was a breach of policy conditions.

rules.reference: Indian Partnership Act, 1932
rules.relevance: Entitles a partner or their representative to have the firm's property applied to debts and surplus distributed, establishing the right to sue for accounts upon dissolution.

rules.case_name: Smt. Premlata & Anr. v. Mis Ishwar Dass Chamanlal & Ors.
rules.reference: Smt. Premlata & Anr. v. Mis Ishwar Dass Chamanlal & Ors.
rules.relevance: Established that legal representatives can enforce arbitration agreements and that the right to sue survives.

rules.reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
rules.relevance: Provides that an arbitration agreement is not discharged by the death of any party and is enforceable by or against the legal representative of the deceased.

rules.reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
rules.relevance: Defines 'legal representative' as a person who in law represents the estate of a deceased person.

rules.case_name: Khardah Company Ltd. v. Raymon & Company (India) Pvt. Ltd.
rules.reference: Khardah Company Ltd. v. Raymon & Company (India) Pvt. Ltd.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent for the principle that an arbitration clause cannot be enforced if the agreement of which it forms an integral part is held to be illegal or void, and that such declarations are within the jurisdiction of the Civil Court.

rules.case_name: A.P.M. Mayankutti v. Secretary, Public Service Department
rules.reference: A.P.M. Mayankutti v. Secretary, Public Service Department
rules.relevance: Held that emergency appointments under Rule 10(a)(i)(1) cannot be taken into account for seniority.

rules.case_name: State of Tamil Nadu v. E. Paripoomam
rules.reference: State of Tamil Nadu v. E. Paripoomam
rules.relevance: Held that temporary appointments under Rule 10(a)(i)(1) are otherwise than in accordance with rules and do not count for seniority.

rules.reference: Andhra Pradesh Panchayat Raj Engineering Service Rules
rules.relevance: Specifies that appointments to Assistant Executive Engineer must be by direct recruitment or transfer, excluding the mode used for temporary appointees.

rules.reference: Andhra Pradesh State and Subordinate Service Rules
rules.relevance: States that temporary appointees under Rule 10(a)(i)(1) shall not be regarded as probationers and are not entitled to preferential claims to future appointments.

rules.case_name: Direct Recruits Class II Officers Association v. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: Direct Recruits Class II Officers Association v. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: Established that appointment in accordance with rules is a condition precedent to counting seniority.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Slum Areas (Improvement, Clearance and Redevelopment) Act, 1971
rules.relevance: The court interpreted this section to determine the SRA's power to remove a developer for contravention of plans, conditions, or time limits, holding it applicable even when the developer holds a power of attorney from the owner-society.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Slum Areas (Improvement, Clearance and Redevelopment) Act, 1971
rules.relevance: The court cited these clauses to affirm the SRA's duty and power to get the slum rehabilitation scheme implemented and to take necessary acts for achieving rehabilitation objectives.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Slum Areas (Improvement, Clearance and Re-development) Act, 1971
rules.relevance: The SRA is empowered to permit redevelopment but must follow statutory procedures, including verifying developer qualifications, financial capacity, and consent of slum dwellers before issuing an LOI.

rules.reference: Development Control Regulations for Greater Bombay, 1991 (as amended in 1997)
rules.relevance: The court held that under the amended DCR, obtaining consent from 70% of eligible slum dwellers is mandatory for a rehabilitation scheme to be considered for approval.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Slum Areas (Improvement, Clearance and Redevelopment) Act, 1971
rules.relevance: The court considered the Slum Act as beneficial welfare legislation that takes precedence over private lease claims to protect the fundamental right to shelter of slum dwellers.

rules.case_name: State of Kerala v. Rajesh
rules.reference: State of Kerala v. Rajesh
rules.relevance: Reiterates the principles guiding the grant of bail in cases under the NDPS Act.

rules.case_name: Preet Pal Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
rules.reference: Preet Pal Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh
rules.relevance: Establishes that post-conviction bail requires strong and compelling reasons and consideration of the prima facie merits of the appeal, as the presumption of innocence no longer applies after a conviction.

rules.case_name: Supreme Court Legal Aid Committee v. Union of India
rules.reference: Supreme Court Legal Aid Committee v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Held that refusing bail while delaying trial is unfair and contrary to Article 21; deprivation of liberty beyond half the maximum punishment violates fundamental rights.

rules.case_name: Dadu v. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: Dadu v. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to clarify that while Section 32-A of the NDPS Act was held ultra vires to the extent it removed the power to suspend sentence, the power to suspend sentence remains strictly subject to the conditions laid down in Section 37 of the Act.

rules.case_name: Dadu alias Tulsidas v. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: Dadu alias Tulsidas v. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: Relied upon to support the proposition that suspension of sentence by an appellate court must be within the parameters of law prescribed by the legislature.

rules.reference: Companies Act, 2013
rules.relevance: Defines the jurisdiction of Special Courts, leading the Court to conclude that the High Court of Delhi lacked jurisdiction to entertain the habeas corpus petition as the accused were produced before the Special Court in Gurugram.

rules.case_name: Kanu Sanyal vs. District Magistrate, Darjeeling and Others
rules.reference: Kanu Sanyal vs. District Magistrate, Darjeeling and Others
rules.relevance: Established that in habeas corpus proceedings, the legality of detention is examined as of the date of the return or hearing, and initial infirmities do not invalidate subsequent valid detention based on judicial orders.

rules.reference: Companies Act, 2013
rules.relevance: Confers power of arrest on SFIO officers, which the Court held is not circumscribed by the time limit for submitting the investigation report.

rules.reference: Companies Act, 2013
rules.relevance: Establishes that upon assignment to SFIO, no other agency can investigate, implying an absolute and irrevocable transfer of investigative powers that does not revert upon the expiry of a time limit.

rules.case_name: Manubhai Ratilal Patel through Ushaben vs. State of Gujarat and others
rules.reference: Manubhai Ratilal Patel through Ushaben vs. State of Gujarat and others
rules.relevance: Held that a writ of habeas corpus is not maintainable against an order of remand passed by a competent Magistrate, as remand is a judicial function.

rules.reference: Strict adherence to age limits
rules.relevance: The court held that age limits prescribed by government rules are mandatory and cannot be relaxed by internal file notings issued after the advertisement.

rules.case_name: State of Karnataka and others v. M.L. Kesari and others
rules.reference: State of Karnataka and others v. M.L. Kesari and others
rules.relevance: Clarifies that for regularization, the appointment must not be illegal. Appointments made against non-sanctioned posts or by persons lacking requisite qualifications are illegal, whereas those made without open competition but with qualifications and sanctioned posts are irregular.

rules.reference: Kerala State Higher Judicial Services Special Rules, 1961
rules.relevance: Establishes that one-third of permanent posts are reserved for direct recruitment, implying a corresponding two-thirds quota for appointment by transfer/promotion.

rules.reference: Kerala State Higher Judicial Services Special Rules, 1961
rules.relevance: Provides that seniority is determined by the date of first appointment, and for simultaneous appointments, by the serial order in the appointment order.

rules.case_name: P. K. Haneefa v. State of Kerala
rules.reference: P. K. Haneefa v. State of Kerala
rules.relevance: Held that Rule 2(b) creates a mandatory quota for direct recruitment and consequently a quota for in-service candidates; appointments in excess of quota do not confer superior seniority.

rules.reference: Credibility of Afterthought Explanations
rules.relevance: An explanation for receiving money that is not offered at the time of recovery, nor in the trial statement, nor during cross-examination, is considered an afterthought and lacks credibility.

rules.reference: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988 (applicable as Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 at the time)
rules.relevance: Defines the offense of public servant accepting gratification other than legal remuneration. The court maintained the conviction under this section.

rules.reference: Sentence Modification based on Delay and Ends of Justice
rules.relevance: In cases involving significant delay in proceedings and where the accused has already undergone substantial imprisonment, the court may reduce the sentence to the period already undergone to meet the ends of justice.

rules.reference: Sentencing discretion based on special circumstances
rules.relevance: The court considers factors such as advanced age, excessive delay in trial, retirement from service, and time already served as 'special reasons' to modify the sentence to meet the ends of justice.

rules.reference: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947
rules.relevance: Section 5(3) prescribes a minimum sentence of one year imprisonment. However, the proviso allows the court to impose a sentence of less than one year for any special reasons recorded in writing.

rules.case_name: Deepa E. V. vs. Union of India and ors.
rules.reference: Deepa E. V. vs. Union of India and ors.
rules.relevance: Distinguished Jitendra Kumar Singh, holding that where government orders expressly bar migration for candidates availing relaxation, such candidates cannot be treated as general category.

rules.reference: Office Memorandum dated 01.07.1998 issued by the Department of Personnel & Training
rules.relevance: The court relied on this OM to establish that candidates selected using relaxed standards (such as lower qualifying marks) must be counted against reserved vacancies and are ineligible for unreserved vacancies.

rules.case_name: Jitendra Kumar Singh vs. State of U.P.
rules.reference: Jitendra Kumar Singh vs. State of U.P.
rules.relevance: Distinguished because it was based on a specific statutory scheme (U.P. Act 1994) that did not contain an express bar on migration for those availing age relaxation, unlike the Rajasthan circulars.

rules.case_name: Jitendra Kumar Singh & Anr. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors.
rules.reference: Jitendra Kumar Singh & Anr. v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors.
rules.relevance: Held that relaxations in eligibility criteria (like age or fees) do not amount to concessions in the recruitment process and do not bar migration to unreserved vacancies.

rules.case_name: Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education & Research, Chandigarh vs. Faculty Association and others
rules.reference: Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education & Research, Chandigarh vs. Faculty Association and others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to overrule the reasoning in K.L. Narsimhan case regarding reservation in single post cadres and to establish that the earlier judgment was set aside.

rules.reference: Railways Act, 1989
rules.relevance: Defines 'untoward incident' to include the accidental falling of a passenger from a train carrying passengers.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. Rina Devi
rules.reference: Union of India v. Rina Devi
rules.relevance: Held that the initial burden of proving bona fide passenger status lies with the claimant, but mere absence of a ticket does not negative the claim; also clarified compensation calculation principles.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. Radha Yadav
rules.reference: Union of India v. Radha Yadav
rules.relevance: Reaffirmed that claimants are entitled to the higher of the compensation amount applicable on the date of accident (with interest) or the amount prescribed on the date of award.

rules.case_name: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Sunil Kumar
rules.reference: United India Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Sunil Kumar
rules.relevance: Laid down that plea of negligence of the victim cannot be allowed in claims based on 'no fault theory'.

rules.reference: Railway Accidents and Untoward Incidents (Compensation) Rules, 1990
rules.relevance: Prescribes the quantum of compensation, which was amended in 2017, creating a conflict regarding the applicable rate.

rules.case_name: Sudhir Chandra Sarkar v. Tata Iron and Steel Co. Ltd. & Ors.
rules.reference: Sudhir Chandra Sarkar v. Tata Iron and Steel Co. Ltd. & Ors.
rules.relevance: Held that termination of service by accepted resignation amounts to retirement for the purpose of gratuity/pension eligibility when the employee has rendered qualifying service.

rules.reference: Interpretation of Beneficial Statutes
rules.relevance: Statutes granting benefits like pension should be interpreted broadly to fulfill legislative intent rather than narrowly to defeat the purpose.

rules.reference: General Insurance (Employees') Pension Scheme, 1995
rules.relevance: Stipulates that resignation entails forfeiture of past service and disqualification for pensionary benefits.

rules.reference: Punjab Civil Services Rules Volume II (as applicable in Haryana)
rules.relevance: This rule governs the condonation of interruption in service. It stipulates that interruption may be condoned only if it does not exceed one year's duration and is caused by reasons beyond the employee's control. The court found the appellant's six-year break exceeded this limit.

rules.reference: General Insurance (Employees') Pension Scheme, 1995
rules.relevance: Provides for pension on voluntary retirement for employees with 20 years of qualifying service who give at least 90 days' notice.

rules.reference: The Consumer Protection Act, 1986
rules.relevance: Provides an exception to the commercial purpose exclusion for services availed exclusively for earning livelihood by means of self-employment.

rules.reference: The Consumer Protection Act, 1986
rules.relevance: Defines 'consumer' and excludes persons who avail services for any 'commercial purpose'.

rules.case_name: Lilavati Kirtilal Mehta Medical Trust v. Unique Shanti Developers
rules.reference: Lilavati Kirtilal Mehta Medical Trust v. Unique Shanti Developers
rules.relevance: Laid down principles for determining 'commercial purpose', emphasizing the dominant intention of profit generation versus personal use.

rules.reference: Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 (SARFAESI Act)
rules.relevance: The court analyzed these sections to determine the limited jurisdiction of the DRAT. Section 17 allows applications against measures taken by secured creditors. Section 19 provides for compensation to borrowers if possession is returned, but does not empower the tribunal to grant liberty for third-party suits. Section 34 bars civil court jurisdiction over matters within the tribunal's domain, emphasizing the exclusive nature of the tribunal's powers.

rules.reference: Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 (RDB Act)
rules.relevance: Section 19(25) allows tribunals to make orders necessary to give effect to their decisions or prevent abuse of process, but does not confer inherent powers. Section 22 states that tribunals are not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure but are guided by principles of natural justice, reinforcing their specialized and limited role.

rules.case_name: Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Hardeep Singh v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: The Supreme Court relied on the parameters established in this Constitution Bench judgment to determine whether the evidence on record was strong, trustworthy, and sufficient to justify summoning the appellant under Section 319 Cr.P.C.

rules.reference: Standard of Satisfaction under Section 319 CrPC
rules.relevance: The court must form a prima facie opinion based on evidence that is more than mere probability but does not require satisfaction that the evidence, if unrebutted, would lead to conviction.

rules.case_name: Joginder Singh & Anr. v. State of Punjab & Anr.
rules.reference: Joginder Singh & Anr. v. State of Punjab & Anr.
rules.relevance: Established that a Court can add any person not accused before it as an accused if sufficient evidence indicates involvement during trial.

rules.case_name: Rakesh & Anr. v. State of Haryana
rules.reference: Rakesh & Anr. v. State of Haryana
rules.relevance: Held that 'evidence' in Section 319 is comprehensive and includes prima facie material from examination-in-chief, allowing the power to be exercised before cross-examination is complete.

rules.case_name: Jarnail Singh and Others v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Jarnail Singh and Others v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: Establishes that the testimony of an injured witness has special evidentiary status and cannot be rejected lightly.

rules.case_name: Keshardeo Chamria v. Radha Kissan Chamria
rules.reference: Keshardeo Chamria v. Radha Kissan Chamria
rules.relevance: The court cited this case to reiterate the principle regarding revision for jurisdictional errors.

rules.case_name: Chaube Jagdish Prasad v. Ganga Prasad Chaturvedi
rules.reference: Chaube Jagdish Prasad v. Ganga Prasad Chaturvedi
rules.relevance: The court cited this case to further support the settled principle regarding revision for jurisdictional errors.

rules.case_name: Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai
rules.reference: Surya Dev Rai v. Ram Chander Rai
rules.relevance: The court cited this case to establish the principle that jurisdictional errors by subordinate courts are subject to superintendence under Article 227.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: The court analyzed these rules to determine that an order refusing to adjudicate on jurisdictional grounds does not constitute a 'deemed decree' under Rule 103, as no actual adjudication of rights occurred.

rules.case_name: Ghasi Ram v. Chait Ram Saini
rules.reference: Ghasi Ram v. Chait Ram Saini
rules.relevance: The court cited this case to confirm that post-1976 amendment, all questions regarding right, title, and interest must be adjudicated by the executing court itself.

rules.case_name: V.S. Palanichamy Chettiar Firm v. C. Alagappan
rules.reference: V.S. Palanichamy Chettiar Firm v. C. Alagappan
rules.relevance: Distinguished on facts; in that case, there was a significant delay in depositing the balance consideration, whereas in the present case, the deposit was made shortly after the appellate decree.

rules.reference: Self-operative conditional decree
rules.relevance: The court applied the principle that if a decree is conditional and self-operative, failure to comply with the conditions within the stipulated time results in the suit being deemed dismissed automatically, leaving no decree to execute.

rules.case_name: Kumar Dhirendra Mullick and Others v. Tivoli Park Apartments (P) Ltd.
rules.reference: Kumar Dhirendra Mullick and Others v. Tivoli Park Apartments (P) Ltd.
rules.relevance: Held that a decree for specific performance is preliminary in nature, the contract is not extinguished, and the court retains jurisdiction to extend time or rescind the agreement.

rules.case_name: K. Kalpana Saraswathi v. P.S.S. Somasundaram Chettiar
rules.reference: K. Kalpana Saraswathi v. P.S.S. Somasundaram Chettiar
rules.relevance: Established that the court has the power under Section 28 to extend time for deposit and that specific performance is an equitable relief requiring the party seeking it to do equity.

rules.case_name: Md. Alimuddin v. Waizuddin and Anr.
rules.reference: Md. Alimuddin v. Waizuddin and Anr.
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this case because in Md. Alimuddin, an application for extension was granted, whereas in the present case, the application was dismissed on merits due to lack of evidence of effort.

rules.case_name: Prahlad Singh Bhati Vs. NCT of Delhi
rules.reference: Prahlad Singh Bhati Vs. NCT of Delhi
rules.relevance: Establishes that bail decisions must consider the nature of accusations, evidence, severity of punishment, and character of the accused.

rules.reference: Recording of vital witnesses before bail
rules.relevance: The court held it is expedient to consider bail after ensuring statements of vital witnesses are recorded to prevent tampering or influence.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The offences alleged in the FIR, the seriousness of which (particularly rape under Section 376) was a key factor in the bail decision.

rules.case_name: Mahipal v. Rajesh Kumar and Anr.
rules.reference: Mahipal v. Rajesh Kumar and Anr.
rules.relevance: Establishes that the Supreme Court may interfere with a High Court's bail order if discretion was exercised without due application of mind or in contravention of law.

rules.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
rules.relevance: This section empowers the High Court to grant bail, but the discretion must be exercised judiciously based on settled principles.

rules.case_name: Trimukh Maruti Kirkan v. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: Trimukh Maruti Kirkan v. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: The court relied on this case for the principle that failure by a husband to explain his wife's death when they were last seen together is a strong circumstance of guilt.

rules.reference: Circumstantial Evidence and Corroboration
rules.relevance: The court relied on the principle that a chain of circumstantial evidence, including extra-judicial confession, recovery of weapons, and 'last seen' testimony, must be complete and corroborated to sustain a conviction.

rules.reference: Chain of circumstantial evidence must be complete
rules.relevance: The court applied this principle to determine if the prosecution had proved the case beyond reasonable doubt through a complete chain of circumstances.

rules.case_name: Bhimapa Chandappa Hosamani v. State of Karnataka
rules.reference: Bhimapa Chandappa Hosamani v. State of Karnataka
rules.relevance: Established that proving motive is not mandatory for conviction if the case is proved beyond reasonable doubt.

rules.reference: False version and subsequent conduct indicate guilty mind
rules.relevance: The court relied on the appellant's false report of suicide and his absconding as strong indicators of guilt.

rules.case_name: Sandeep Khanduja v. Atul Dande
rules.reference: Sandeep Khanduja v. Atul Dande
rules.relevance: Clarified that the percentage of permanent disability is not automatically the percentage of economic loss; the impact on earning capacity must be assessed based on the victim's vocation.

rules.case_name: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
rules.reference: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.
rules.relevance: Established that the benefit of future prospects extends to self-employed individuals and those on fixed salaries, warranting an addition to income for compensation calculation.

rules.case_name: Jagdish v. Mohan & Ors.
rules.reference: Jagdish v. Mohan & Ors.
rules.relevance: Confirmed that the addition for future prospects applies to injury cases involving permanent disablement, not just death cases.

rules.reference: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988
rules.relevance: Provides the statutory basis for claiming compensation for injuries caused by rash and negligent driving.

rules.reference: No deduction for personal expenses in injury cases
rules.relevance: Unlike fatal accident cases involving loss of dependency, no deduction for personal and living expenses is required when calculating loss of future earnings for an injured claimant.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code (IPC)
rules.relevance: These sections define the offences of unlawful assembly, rioting, trespass, and murder, under which the appellants were convicted.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: Charges related to unlawful assembly and rioting which were held not proved, impacting the logical sustainability of the murder conviction for only two accused.

rules.reference: Sifting the chaff from the grain
rules.relevance: The principle that courts should separate reliable testimony from unreliable parts, unless discrepancies are material and shake the witness's credibility entirely.

rules.case_name: Arvind Kumar @ Nemichand & Ors. vs. State of Rajasthan
rules.reference: Arvind Kumar @ Nemichand & Ors. vs. State of Rajasthan
rules.relevance: Cited for the proposition that 'falsus in uno falsus in omnibus' is a rule of caution, not strict law, and that evidence must be rejected if discrepancies are material and inseparable.

rules.case_name: Masalti v. State of Uttar Pradesh
rules.reference: Masalti v. State of Uttar Pradesh
rules.relevance: Clarified that membership in an unlawful assembly with a common object creates vicarious liability under Section 149 IPC.

rules.case_name: Secretary, State of Karnataka v. Umadev
rules.reference: Secretary, State of Karnataka v. Umadev
rules.relevance: Distinguished between regularization (impermissible) and pay parity (permissible), holding that daily-wagers are entitled to the minimum wage of the regular cadre if they perform the same work.

rules.case_name: State of U.P. v. Putti Lal
rules.reference: State of U.P. v. Putti Lal
rules.relevance: Held that daily-wagers discharging similar duties are entitled to the minimum of the pay scale, though not necessarily allowances or increments.

rules.reference: University Grants Commission (UGC) Recommendations
rules.relevance: Established the benchmark pay scale for Lecturers/Assistant Professors which served as the reference point for the entitlement of Research Assistants.

rules.case_name: Bindeshwari Prasad Singh & Others v. State of Rajasthan & Others

rules.reference: K. Ramadas Shenoy v. Chief Officers, Town Municipal Council
rules.relevance: Established that municipal authorities have a statutory duty to prevent unauthorized constructions that violate planned development and residential rights.

rules.case_name: Shanti Sports Club v. Union of India
rules.reference: Shanti Sports Club v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Emphasized zero tolerance for illegal constructions and that no compromise should be made with town planning schemes.

rules.relevance: The court applied the principle that illegal constructions cannot be regularized if they violate sanctioned plans, defy statutory notices, or pose public safety hazards.

rules.reference: Kolkata Municipal Corporation Act, 1980
rules.relevance: Empowers the Mayor-in-Council to order the demolition of unauthorized constructions that pose a hazard or violate sanctioned plans.

rules.reference: Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax Act, 2006
rules.relevance: The provision denying ITC for inter-state sales under Section 8(2) of the CST Act, which was challenged and subsequently read down by the Court.

rules.case_name: R.C. Tobacco Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India
rules.reference: R.C. Tobacco Pvt. Ltd. v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Cited for the principle that a retrospective fiscal statute is not unreasonable merely because it operates retrospectively, but it must not be unduly oppressive, confiscatory, or impose an unforeseeable financial burden.

rules.reference: Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax Act, 2006
rules.relevance: Defined State Government as a dealer but exempted it from registration, leading the Court to read down Section 19(5)(c) for sales to State Governments.

rules.case_name: Jayam and Company vs. Assistant Commissioner and Another
rules.reference: Jayam and Company vs. Assistant Commissioner and Another
rules.relevance: Established that Input Tax Credit is a statutory concession, not a vested right, and conditions for availing it must be strictly complied with to prevent tax evasion.

rules.reference: Tamil Nadu Value Added Tax Rules, 2007
rules.relevance: The rule requiring Form C for claiming ITC on inter-state sales, challenged alongside Section 19(5)(c).

rules.case_name: Man Kaur v. Hartar Singh Sangha
rules.reference: Man Kaur v. Hartar Singh Sangha
rules.relevance: Establishes that a power of attorney holder cannot depose in place of the principal.

rules.case_name: MIS Shankar Finance and Investment v. State of A.P & Ors.
rules.reference: MIS Shankar Finance and Investment v. State of A.P & Ors.
rules.relevance: Establishes that a power of attorney holder cannot depose in place of the principal.

rules.case_name: Vidhyadhar v. Manikrao & Anr.
rules.reference: Vidhyadhar v. Manikrao & Anr.
rules.relevance: Establishes that a power of attorney holder cannot depose in place of the principal.

rules.case_name: Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt. Ltd.(2) vs. State of Haryana & Anr.
rules.reference: Suraj Lamp & Industries Pvt. Ltd.(2) vs. State of Haryana & Anr.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to establish that SA/GPA/WILL transactions do not convey title or create interest in immovable property and are not valid modes of transfer.

rules.reference: Effect of General Power of Attorney on Possession
rules.relevance: The court considered that a registered GPA, supported by witness testimony, is sufficient evidence to establish possession for the purpose of an injunction suit, even if it does not confer title.

rules.reference: The National Human Rights Commission Chairperson and Members (Salaries, Allowances and other Conditions of Service) Rules, 1993
rules.relevance: Limits the total encashment of earned leave from current and previous service to a maximum of 240 days.

rules.case_name: Subedar Harpal Singh, Retd. Vs. State of Haryana and Another
rules.reference: Subedar Harpal Singh, Retd. Vs. State of Haryana and Another
rules.relevance: The court referred to this judgment to support the interpretation of Rule 4.23 as applicable in Haryana, confirming that breaks not meeting the specific conditions of the rule cannot be condoned.

rules.reference: Punjab Civil Services Rules Volume II (as applicable in Haryana)
rules.relevance: This rule governs the condonation of interruption in service. It stipulates that interruption may be condoned only if it does not exceed one year's duration and is caused by reasons beyond the employee's control. The court found the appellant's six-year break exceeded this limit.

rules.reference: The National Human Rights Commission Chairperson and Members (Salaries, Allowances and other Conditions of Service) Rules, 1993
rules.relevance: Stipulates that a Member's salary equals that of a Supreme Court Judge, subject to deduction of pension received for previous service under the Government of the Union or a State.

rules.reference: Punjab Civil Services Rules Volume II (as applicable in Haryana)
rules.relevance: This rule allows commuting periods of absence without leave into leave without allowances. The court distinguished this from Rule 4.23, noting it does not apply to breaks in service caused by voluntary retirement.

rules.reference: Central Sales Tax Act, 1956
rules.relevance: This provision explicitly empowers the State Government to make rules for 'the time within which' changes in business details are furnished. The court used this to distinguish 'manner' from 'time'.

rules.reference: Central Sales Tax Act, 1956
rules.relevance: This provision empowers the State Government to make rules regarding the authority, conditions, and manner in which declarations are furnished. The court examined if this included prescribing time limits.

rules.case_name: Acraman v. Herniman
rules.reference: Acraman v. Herniman
rules.relevance: The court relied on this case for the proposition that 'manner and form' does not introduce time limits from a referenced Act.

rules.reference: Interpretation of 'manner and form'
rules.relevance: The principle that 'manner and form' refers only to the mode in which an act is to be done and does not include time limits unless explicitly stated.

rules.reference: Central Sales Tax (Kerala) Rules
rules.relevance: This rule imposed a specific deadline (February 16, 1961) for filing pending declarations. The court had to determine if this rule was valid under the Act.

rules.case_name: Pioneer Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd. v. Govindan Raghavan
rules.reference: Pioneer Urban Land & Infrastructure Ltd. v. Govindan Raghavan
rules.relevance: Established that one-sided contractual terms constitute an unfair trade practice and that inordinate delay amounts to deficiency of service.

rules.case_name: M/s Imperia Structures Ltd. v. Anil Patni and Anr
rules.reference: M/s Imperia Structures Ltd. v. Anil Patni and Anr
rules.relevance: Held that remedies under the Consumer Protection Act are in addition to those under the RERA Act, and allottees have a choice of forum.

rules.reference: Haryana Fire Safety Act, 2009
rules.relevance: Mandates obtaining Fire NOC before commencement of construction for high-rise buildings, establishing it as a pre-condition for the possession timeline.

rules.case_name: Attorney-General v. British Broadcasting Corporation
rules.reference: Attorney-General v. British Broadcasting Corporation
rules.relevance: Established that the object of contempt of court is to protect the administration of justice, not the dignity of the courts or judges.

rules.case_name: Himanshu Arora v. DLF Homes Panchkula Pvt. Ltd.
rules.citation: Civil Appeal Nos. 11097-11138 of 2018, decided on 19.11.2018
rules.reference: Himanshu Arora v. DLF Homes Panchkula Pvt. Ltd.
rules.relevance: The court relied on the directions issued in this earlier case to determine the rate of interest (9%) and the modalities for computing compensation and refunds in the present batch of appeals.

rules.case_name: Rajeev Kourav v. Baisahab & Ors.
rules.reference: Rajeev Kourav v. Baisahab & Ors.
rules.relevance: Holds that statements under Section 161 Cr.P.C. are inadmissible in evidence and cannot form the basis for quashing proceedings.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Employees of Private Schools Act, 1977
rules.relevance: The statutory provision under which the respondent filed an appeal before the School Tribunal against his termination.
