rules.relevance: The court held that departmental inquiries operate on the principle of preponderance of probability and are independent of criminal trials, which require proof beyond reasonable doubt; thus, pending criminal cases do not justify withholding a decision in departmental matters.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Employees of Private Schools (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1981
rules.relevance: Rules cited by the Inquiry Committee members to argue that deciding the case pending criminal proceedings would amount to contempt of court, which the Supreme Court rejected.

rules.case_name: State of Punjab and Ors. vs. Dr. Harbhajan Singh Greasy
rules.reference: State of Punjab and Ors. vs. Dr. Harbhajan Singh Greasy
rules.relevance: Cited by the Tribunal to support remitting the matter for fresh consideration if the inquiry is found faulty; the Supreme Court distinguished the context, noting the fault here was the refusal to decide rather than procedural error.

rules.reference: Karnataka Selection of Candidates for Admission to Engineering, Medical, Dental, Pharmacy and Nursing Courses Rules, 1993
rules.relevance: The court examined the 1995 amendments to these rules which restricted admissions to Karnataka students, and directed that the restriction not operate for the current academic year.

rules.case_name: Dr. Dinesh Kumar and Others v. Motilal Nehru Medical College, Allahabad and Others
rules.reference: Dr. Dinesh Kumar and Others v. Motilal Nehru Medical College, Allahabad and Others
rules.relevance: The court analyzed the scheme formulated in this case to determine its applicability to private colleges, concluding that State quota seats in private colleges are subject to Article 14 principles.

rules.reference: Information Bulletins for Post Graduate Entrance Test-2014 (PGET-2014)
rules.relevance: The specific clause defining 'Karnataka Origin' was challenged and declared ultra vires Article 14 by the court.

rules.reference: Constitution of India, Article 371D
rules.relevance: The court held that the Governor's notification cannot override the Presidential Order issued under Article 371D regarding local cadres and equitable opportunities in Andhra Pradesh.

rules.case_name: Nikhil Himthani v. State of Uttarakhand & Others
rules.reference: Nikhil Himthani v. State of Uttarakhand & Others
rules.relevance: The court quoted this case to reinforce the principle that merit must be the test for selection in higher education and that residential reservations affect equality of opportunity under Article 14.

rules.reference: C.P.C.B. rules and norms
rules.relevance: The court directed the strict enforcement of Central Pollution Control Board norms regarding prevention of pollution at construction sites.

rules.reference: Rules regarding solid waste management
rules.relevance: The court directed authorities to refrain from burning solid waste and to follow relevant rules for scientific disposal.

rules.case_name: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India and Others
rules.reference: M.C. Mehta v. Union of India and Others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to support the principle that vehicles not bound for Delhi should be diverted to alternative routes to reduce pollution, citing the spirit of the earlier order.

rules.reference: Judicial direction to mitigate environmental hardship
rules.relevance: The court exercised its powers to issue specific directions on traffic diversion, entry charges, and vehicle bans to mitigate high pollution levels in Delhi.

rules.case_name: National Human Rights Commission vs. State of Arunachal Pradesh
rules.reference: National Human Rights Commission vs. State of Arunachal Pradesh
rules.relevance: Cited for the duty of the State to protect the life and liberty of persons against threats from private groups.

rules.reference: Lapse of time between injury and death
rules.relevance: The court determined that the time gap between the infliction of injury and death is not a determinative factor for reducing liability from murder to culpable homicide if the injury was sufficient to cause death.

rules.case_name: K.M. Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: K.M. Nanavati v. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: Defined the standard for 'grave and sudden provocation' under Exception 1 to Section 300, emphasizing the test of a reasonable man and the cooling down period.

rules.case_name: State Of Andhra Pradesh v. Rayavarapu Punnayya & Anr.
rules.reference: State Of Andhra Pradesh v. Rayavarapu Punnayya & Anr.
rules.relevance: Clarified the distinction between Section 299 and Section 300, particularly regarding the degree of probability of death and the meaning of 'sufficient in the ordinary course of nature'.

rules.reference: Credibility of eyewitnesses related to the deceased
rules.relevance: The court held that the relationship of witnesses to the deceased does not per se exclude their testimony if it is corroborated and credible.

rules.case_name: Rajendra Singh & Ors. v. State of Bihar
rules.reference: Rajendra Singh & Ors. v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: Established that Exception 4 requires a sudden fight, absence of premeditation, and no undue advantage or cruelty, and cannot be a cloak for pre-existing malice.

rules.case_name: Jarnail Singh and Others v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Jarnail Singh and Others v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: Establishes that the testimony of an injured witness has special evidentiary status and cannot be rejected lightly.

rules.reference: Fair and Impartial Investigation
rules.relevance: The court found the investigation tainted due to interpolation in FIR, doubtful recoveries, and failure to record statements of material witnesses promptly.

rules.reference: Necessity of Test Identification Parade
rules.relevance: The court held that the failure to hold a test identification parade when witnesses did not know the assailants' names was a serious lacuna in the prosecution case.

rules.case_name: Raghav Prapanna Tripathi vs. The State Of Uttar Pradesh
rules.reference: Raghav Prapanna Tripathi vs. The State Of Uttar Pradesh
rules.relevance: Established that the mere presence of blood stains on an object does not conclusively prove it is human blood or belongs to the victim.

rules.case_name: Kansa Behera vs. State of Orissa
rules.reference: Kansa Behera vs. State of Orissa
rules.relevance: Held that serology reports finding human blood are insufficient without evidence connecting it to the deceased.

rules.case_name: Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam and others vs. State of Bihar and others
rules.reference: Kahkashan Kausar alias Sonam and others vs. State of Bihar and others
rules.relevance: Supported the view that general omnibus allegations against in-laws in matrimonial disputes, without specific details, amount to misuse of process.

rules.case_name: State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others
rules.reference: State of Haryana and others vs. Bhajan Lal and others
rules.relevance: The court relied on categories (1) and (5) of this judgment to determine that the allegations were insufficient to prima facie constitute an offence and were inherently improbable.

rules.reference: General omnibus allegations in matrimonial disputes
rules.relevance: Vague, general allegations against in-laws without specific instances of harassment constitute an abuse of the process of law.

rules.case_name: Mahmood Ali & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
rules.reference: Mahmood Ali & Ors. v. State of U.P. & Ors.
rules.relevance: The court relied on the principle that the High Court must look into the FIR with care and read between the lines in frivolous or vexatious proceedings.

rules.case_name: Preeti Gupta v. State of Jharkhand

rules.relevance: The court relied on observations regarding the misuse of Section 498A in matrimonial disputes and the need to scrutinize allegations carefully.

rules.reference: Defence of identification to be considered at trial

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The court considered the gravity of the offences, specifically murder under Section 302, to determine that bail was not appropriate at the pre-trial stage.

rules.case_name: Dablu Kujur v. State of Jharkhand

rules.relevance: Crystallized the legal position that chargesheets must contain sufficient details and evidence to enable the Magistrate to take cognizance, not just a reproduction of the FIR.

rules.case_name: T.N. Godavarman Thirumalpad v. Union of India
rules.reference: T.N. Godavarman Thirumalpad v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Established that 'forest' must be understood according to its dictionary meaning, not just statutory notification, for conservation purposes.

rules.case_name: Associated Capsules Private Limited v. Deputy Commissioner of Income Tax

rules.relevance: Crystallized the legal position that chargesheets must contain sufficient details and evidence to enable the Magistrate to take cognizance, not just a reproduction of the FIR.

rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to establish the base market value of Rs. 20 lakhs per acre for lands acquired in 1994.

rules.case_name: Surender Singh v. State of Haryana and others
rules.reference: Surender Singh v. State of Haryana and others
rules.relevance: The court referred to this case to highlight the importance of considering material issues such as location, development, and nature of land when determining fair market rates, rather than applying a uniform rate to disparate villages.

rules.case_name: ONGC Ltd. v. Rameshbhai Jivanbhai Patel
rules.reference: ONGC Ltd. v. Rameshbhai Jivanbhai Patel
rules.relevance: The court relied on the principles regarding annual increase in land value, distinguishing between rural areas (5-7.5% escalation) and urban areas, and noting that post-acquisition sales require higher deductions to work backward to the date of notification.

rules.reference: Indian Telegraph Act, 1885
rules.relevance: The court relied on this provision to determine the appellant's entitlement to compensation for the use of land and damage caused by the erection of towers.

rules.reference: Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002 (SARFAESI Act)
rules.relevance: The court analyzed these sections to determine the limited jurisdiction of the DRAT. Section 17 allows applications against measures taken by secured creditors. Section 19 provides for compensation to borrowers if possession is returned, but does not empower the tribunal to grant liberty for third-party suits. Section 34 bars civil court jurisdiction over matters within the tribunal's domain, emphasizing the exclusive nature of the tribunal's powers.

rules.reference: Tribunals do not possess inherent powers
rules.relevance: The court held that the DRAT could not grant liberty to file a separate suit as it lacked the inherent jurisdiction to do so under the special legislation. Tribunals must function within statutory parameters.

rules.reference: Recovery of Debts Due to Banks and Financial Institutions Act, 1993 (RDB Act)
rules.relevance: Section 19(25) allows tribunals to make orders necessary to give effect to their decisions or prevent abuse of process, but does not confer inherent powers. Section 22 states that tribunals are not bound by the Code of Civil Procedure but are guided by principles of natural justice, reinforcing their specialized and limited role.

rules.reference: Speedy disposal is a fundamental object of SARFAESI and RDB Acts
rules.relevance: The court emphasized that delay in adjudication frustrates the legislative purpose and harms the economic interest of the country, criticizing the DRAT for taking four and a half years to dispose of the appeal.

rules.reference: Security Interest (Enforcement) Rules, 2002
rules.relevance: The court relied on the mandatory requirement of a 30-day notice under these rules, the non-compliance of which justified setting aside the auction sale.

rules.reference: Spontaneity of FIR and external checks
rules.relevance: Courts verify the promptness of an FIR through external checks like Magistrate's receipt and inquest report details to prevent embellishment.

rules.case_name: Gulab Vs. State of U.P.
rules.reference: Credibility of Eyewitnesses vs. Ballistic Evidence
rules.relevance: Non-recovery of a weapon does not discredit the prosecution if eyewitness accounts are credible; however, if eyewitnesses are inconsistent, the lack of ballistic evidence becomes fatal.

rules.case_name: Selvaraj v. The State of Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: Selvaraj v. The State of Tamil Nadu
rules.relevance: Held that concurrent findings of guilt can be set aside if the prosecution story is highly improbable and inconsistent with the ordinary course of human nature.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code
rules.relevance: The substantive offences for which the appellant was convicted by the High Court.

rules.reference: Motive is not sufficient to prove guilt
rules.relevance: Motive alone cannot sustain a conviction without corroborative evidence linking the accused to the crime.

rules.case_name: Ponnala Lakshmaiah v. Kommuri Pratap Reddy
rules.reference: Ponnala Lakshmaiah v. Kommuri Pratap Reddy
rules.relevance: Held that non-compliance with the proviso to Section 83(1) is not fatal to the maintainability of an election petition and that defects are curable.

rules.reference: Conduct of Election Rules, 1961
rules.relevance: Prescribes the specific form of affidavit required to support allegations of corrupt practice in an election petition.

rules.case_name: A. Manju v. Prajwal Revanna
rules.reference: A. Manju v. Prajwal Revanna
rules.relevance: Reinforced that non-submission of Form 25 is a curable defect and the petition should not be dismissed at the threshold if there is substantial compliance.

rules.case_name: G.M. Siddeshwar v. Prasanna Kumar
rules.reference: G.M. Siddeshwar v. Prasanna Kumar
rules.relevance: Establishes that substantial compliance with affidavit formats is sufficient and a composite affidavit can satisfy statutory requirements.

rules.reference: Rules Relating to Election Petitions (Madhya Pradesh High Court)
rules.relevance: Imposes a mandatory duty on the Registrar to sign every page; however, failure to do so is an act of the court and does not prejudice the party.

rules.reference: Mere possibility of abuse does not invalidate legislation
rules.relevance: The core legal principle applied to reject the challenge; a valid statute cannot be struck down merely because it may be misused.

rules.case_name: Budhan Choudhry and Ors. v. State of Bihar
rules.reference: Budhan Choudhry and Ors. v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: Relied upon to hold that a provision is not arbitrary or violative of Article 14 merely because it may be abused by authorities.

rules.reference: Criminal Law (Second Amendment) Act, 1983
rules.relevance: The amending act that introduced Section 498A; its Statement of Objects and Reasons established the intent to combat dowry deaths and cruelty.

rules.case_name: Mafatlal Industries Ltd. and Ors. v. Union of India and Ors.
rules.reference: Mafatlal Industries Ltd. and Ors. v. Union of India and Ors.
rules.relevance: Cited for the observation that mere possibility of abuse of a provision cannot be a ground for holding it procedurally or substantively unreasonable.

rules.case_name: Thangal Kunju Musaliar v. M. Venkatachalam Potti
rules.reference: Thangal Kunju Musaliar v. M. Venkatachalam Potti
rules.relevance: Cited for the principle that administrative application of law should not be done with an evil eye, and mere possibility of abuse does not invalidate legislation.

rules.case_name: Samsher Singh v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Samsher Singh v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: The court relied on this seven-Judge Bench decision to establish that the form of the order is not decisive and that termination based on misconduct without inquiry is punitive.

rules.case_name: State Bank of India v. Palak Modi
rules.reference: State Bank of India v. Palak Modi
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to reject the view in Pavanendra Narayan Verma and affirm that courts can lift the veil of termination simpliciter if founded on misconduct.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. Mahaveer C. Singhvi
rules.reference: Union of India v. Mahaveer C. Singhvi
rules.relevance: The court cited this case to support the principle that if findings of misconduct are arrived at behind the back of the officer, a simple termination order is bad.

rules.reference: Motive vs. Foundation of Termination
rules.relevance: The court applied the test to determine if the termination was punitive (foundation) or simpliciter (motive) based on the Vigilance report.

rules.case_name: Pavanendra Narayan Verma v. Sanjay Gandhi P.G.I. of Medical Sciences
rules.reference: Pavanendra Narayan Verma v. Sanjay Gandhi P.G.I. of Medical Sciences
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this decision, noting its abstract proposition was contrary to Samsher Singh and confined to its facts.

rules.case_name: Trisuns Chemical Industry Vs. Rajesh Agarwal and Ors.
rules.reference: Trisuns Chemical Industry Vs. Rajesh Agarwal and Ors.
rules.relevance: Holds that the existence of an arbitration clause or civil remedy does not preclude criminal prosecution for offences like cheating, as arbitration cannot try criminal acts.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The specific offences alleged in the FIR and charge-sheet, namely cheating, criminal breach of trust, and common intention.

rules.reference: Face Value Test for Quashing
rules.relevance: At the stage of quashing proceedings, the allegations in the FIR/charge-sheet must be taken at their face value without critical examination of their truth or falsity.

rules.reference: Negotiable Instruments Act
rules.relevance: Creates a rebuttable presumption that a cheque was issued for the discharge of a debt or liability; the court held this presumption should not bar criminal proceedings if other offences are disclosed.

rules.case_name: Priyanka Mishra v State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.reference: Quashing of Criminal Proceedings in Civil Disputes
rules.relevance: The court relied on the principle that protection should be accorded against unwanted criminal prosecution when the dispute is essentially civil in nature.

rules.case_name: Basalingappa v. Mudibasapp
rules.reference: Basalingappa v. Mudibasapp
rules.relevance: Holds that the presumption under Section 139 is rebuttable by preponderance of probability.

rules.case_name: Rohitbhai Jivanlal Patel v. State of Gujarat
rules.reference: Rohitbhai Jivanlal Patel v. State of Gujarat
rules.relevance: Establishes that once the signature is proved, the onus shifts to the accused to rebut the presumption under Section 139, and the court cannot question the complainant's evidence on source of funds.

rules.case_name: Narendra Pratap Narain Singh v. State of U.P.
rules.reference: Narendra Pratap Narain Singh v. State of U.P.
rules.relevance: Established the principle that the Supreme Court's jurisdiction under Article 136 to interfere with concurrent findings of fact is limited to cases where findings are based on no evidence or are perverse.

rules.reference: Appellate Court's power to reverse acquittal in Section 138 cases
rules.relevance: The court held that an Appellate Court can reverse an acquittal if the Trial Court's judgment is perverse or suffers from a fundamental error of approach regarding the application of statutory presumptions.

rules.case_name: Arulvelu and Anr. v. State represented by Public Prosecutor & Anr.
rules.reference: Arulvelu and Anr. v. State represented by Public Prosecutor & Anr.
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this case (relating to IPC offences) to hold that the strict restrictions on appellate interference with acquittals do not apply with the same rigour to Section 138 NI Act cases where statutory presumptions are involved.

rules.case_name: Neechu Chopra and another vs. Bharti
rules.reference: Neechu Chopra and another vs. Bharti
rules.relevance: Distinguished on facts: in that case, the husband had died and parents were too old, whereas here the accused are the husband and parents actively alleged to have harassed the wife.

rules.case_name: State of Haryana v. Bhajanlal
rules.reference: State of Haryana v. Bhajanlal
rules.relevance: Laid down parameters for quashing FIRs under Section 482, including when proceedings are manifestly attended with mala fide or result in failure of justice.

rules.case_name: Geeta Mehrotra and another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another
rules.reference: Geeta Mehrotra and another vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another
rules.relevance: Distinguished on facts: involved brother and sister of husband after divorce, whereas present case involves husband and parents during subsistence of marriage.

rules.case_name: Y. Abraham Ajith and Ors. v. Inspector of Police, Chennai and Anr.
rules.reference: Y. Abraham Ajith and Ors. v. Inspector of Police, Chennai and Anr.
rules.relevance: Referred regarding the determination of territorial jurisdiction at the pre-trial stage based on the cause of action.

rules.case_name: Manoj Mahavir Prasad Khaitan vs. Ram Gopal Moddar and another
rules.reference: Manoj Mahavir Prasad Khaitan vs. Ram Gopal Moddar and another
rules.relevance: Distinguished on facts: involved a brother-in-law and allegations of theft found absurd, unlike the direct harassment allegations in the present case.

rules.case_name: JAG Mahender & Anr. Vs. State of Haryana & Ors.
rules.citation: Order dated 21.09.2017 in Civil Appeal No.15702/2017
rules.reference: JAG Mahender & Anr. Vs. State of Haryana & Ors.
rules.relevance: Concludes that a 25% deduction for development charges is justified in similar contexts involving highway construction.

rules.reference: Land Acquisition Act, 1894
rules.relevance: Governs the procedure for notification, declaration, and reference for determination of market value.

rules.case_name: Atma Singh (Dead) through Lrs. and Ors. vs. State of Haryana and Anr.
rules.reference: Atma Singh (Dead) through Lrs. and Ors. vs. State of Haryana and Anr.
rules.relevance: Holds that sale instances of small pieces of land cannot be ignored when determining compensation for large extents, especially if the land has non-agricultural potential.

rules.case_name: Subh Ram & Ors. vs. State of Haryana & Anr.
rules.reference: Subh Ram & Ors. vs. State of Haryana & Anr.
rules.relevance: Established standard deductions of 1/3rd for infrastructure space and 1/3rd for infrastructural costs, totaling 67% for development.

rules.case_name: State of Gujarat vs. Kakhot SinghJi VajesinghJi Vaghela
rules.reference: State of Gujarat vs. Kakhot SinghJi VajesinghJi Vaghela
rules.relevance: Establishes that the price agreed between a willing seller and purchaser represents the market value.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. V. Sriharan @ Murugan & Ors.
rules.reference: Union of India v. V. Sriharan @ Murugan & Ors.
rules.relevance: Established that courts can impose a special category of life sentence (e.g., 30 years without remission) as an alternative to the death penalty in cases that do not fall under the 'rarest of rare' category but where standard life imprisonment is inadequate.

rules.case_name: State of Maharashtra v. Shrinivas Nayak and Another
rules.reference: State of Maharashtra v. Shrinivas Nayak and Another
rules.relevance: Established the principle that the court record must be believed and a party cannot later dispute a statement made by their counsel on instructions.

rules.case_name: Muthuramalingam and others v. State represented by Inspector of Police
rules.reference: Muthuramalingam and others v. State represented by Inspector of Police
rules.relevance: Clarified that consecutive life sentences cannot be awarded as humans have only one life; such sentences must run concurrently.

rules.case_name: R.K. Anand v. Delhi High Court
rules.reference: R.K. Anand v. Delhi High Court
rules.relevance: Established that prohibiting an advocate from appearing in court for a specified period is a valid punishment for criminal contempt to protect the purity of court proceedings.

rules.reference: Supreme Court Guidelines to Regulate Conferment of Designation of Senior Advocates, 2018
rules.relevance: The operational guidelines implementing the 2017 Judgment, which are subject to the modifications made in the present judgment.

rules.case_name: Virgo Industries (Eng.) Private Limited v. Venturetech Solutions Private Limited
rules.reference: Virgo Industries (Eng.) Private Limited v. Venturetech Solutions Private Limited
rules.relevance: Reiterated that Order 2 Rule 2 discourages vexing the defendant with multiple suits and that leave is required to sue for omitted reliefs.

rules.case_name: Ramesh Chand Ardawatiya v. Anil Panjwani
rules.reference: Ramesh Chand Ardawatiya v. Anil Panjwani
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this precedent, noting it did not address whether a counter-claim can be filed after trial conclusion or solely against a co-defendant.

rules.case_name: Mohd. Khalil Khan v. Mahbub Ali Mian

rules.relevance: Established the test for determining if a new suit is founded on a cause of action distinct from the former suit.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: The court held that a decree on default under this rule was unsustainable because the trial court never formally treated the amended written statement as a counter-claim or directed the other parties to file an answer.

rules.reference: Counter-claim must be directed against the plaintiff
rules.relevance: The court established that a counter-claim directed solely against co-defendants, without any claim against the plaintiff, cannot be maintained and cannot convert litigation into an inter-pleader suit.

rules.case_name: Mobilox Innovations Private Limited v. Kirusa Software Private Limited
rules.reference: Mobilox Innovations Private Limited v. Kirusa Software Private Limited
rules.relevance: Established that the IBC is not a substitute for a recovery forum and that the existence of a real dispute precludes the invocation of IBC provisions.

rules.reference: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
rules.relevance: Governs the initiation of CIRP by an operational creditor; requires the debt to be undisputed.

rules.reference: Existence of a dispute is a bar to initiating CIRP
rules.relevance: The adjudicating authority must reject an application under Section 9 if a notice of dispute has been received or if a dispute exists in fact.

rules.reference: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
rules.relevance: Requires the corporate debtor to notify the operational creditor of any dispute regarding the debt within 10 days of receiving the demand notice.

rules.case_name: Committee of Creditors of Essar Steel India Limited v. Satish Kumar Gupta
rules.reference: Committee of Creditors of Essar Steel India Limited v. Satish Kumar Gupta
rules.relevance: Establishes that a successful resolution applicant cannot be faced with undecided claims after the plan is accepted, as this creates uncertainty.

rules.reference: Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975
rules.relevance: The court directed the Director to execute documents transferring possession and title to plot holders in terms of this provision once development charges are paid.

rules.reference: Recovery of dues as land revenue
rules.relevance: The court directed that outstanding license fees and security expenses be recovered from the colonizer as if they were land revenue if not paid voluntarily.

rules.reference: Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Act, 1975
rules.relevance: The court noted that the licenses for the land were granted under this section, establishing the statutory basis for the Colonizer's initial rights.

rules.reference: Haryana Development and Regulation of Urban Areas Rules, 1976
rules.relevance: The court noted the colonizer's non-compliance with these rules regarding the maintenance of separate ledger accounts and deposit of funds.

rules.reference: NOIDA (Preparation and Finalisation of Plan) Regulations, 1991
rules.relevance: Defines 'Commercial Use' to include hotels and 'Industrial Use' to involve manufacturing/processing; the court used this to determine that hotels are commercial, not industrial, for land use purposes.

rules.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
rules.relevance: Provides that the Board may order transfer of trial to the Children's Court only after determining a need to try the child as an adult.

rules.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
rules.relevance: Defines 'Child in Conflict with Law' (CICL), establishing the appellant's status as a juvenile at the time of the offense.

rules.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015
rules.relevance: Empowers the Children's Court to decide whether there is a need to try the child as an adult after receiving the preliminary assessment from the Board.

rules.case_name: Ajeet Gurjar v. State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.reference: Ajeet Gurjar v. State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.relevance: Held that the procedure under Sections 15 and 19 of the JJ Act is mandatory and the word 'may' in Section 19(1) should be read as 'shall'.

rules.relevance: Distinguished because the plea of juvenility was raised late in that case, unlike the present case where the age was known at the inception of investigation.

rules.reference: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
rules.relevance: The court interpreted these sections to determine that the Act provides a mechanism for inquiry but does not oust the High Court's constitutional power under Article 235.

rules.reference: Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition and Redressal) Act, 2013
rules.relevance: Established that the right of appeal arises only from the final inquiry report under Section 13, not from a preliminary report.

rules.case_name: State of Tamil Nadu Rep. by Secretary to Govt.(Home) Vs. Promod Kumar IPS and Another
rules.reference: State of Tamil Nadu Rep. by Secretary to Govt.(Home) Vs. Promod Kumar IPS and Another
rules.relevance: Distinguished as it pertained to IPS officers, whereas the petitioner is a judicial officer subject to Article 235.

rules.case_name: State of West Bengal and Another Vs. Nripendra Nath Bagchi
rules.reference: State of West Bengal and Another Vs. Nripendra Nath Bagchi
rules.relevance: Established that 'control' under Article 235 includes disciplinary jurisdiction and the power to hold inquiries.

rules.case_name: Malarvizhi & Ors. Vs. United India Insurance CO. Ltd. & Ors.
rules.reference: Malarvizhi & Ors. Vs. United India Insurance CO. Ltd. & Ors.
rules.relevance: Establishes that Income Tax Return is a statutory document to be relied upon for income determination and mandates 9% interest on compensation.

rules.case_name: New India Assurance Company v. Yogesh Devi
rules.reference: New India Assurance Company v. Yogesh Devi
rules.relevance: Distinguished because it dealt with a case lacking evidence of income; here, income tax returns were available. Also established that evidence must be adduced to compute depletion in net income.

rules.reference: United India Insurance Company Limited v. Satinder Kaur & Ors.

rules.reference: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanu Ram
rules.relevance: The court referred to this judgment to interpret 'consortium' as a compendious term encompassing spousal, parental, and filial consortium.

rules.case_name: National Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors.

rules.relevance: Held that concurrent findings of fact by the Regulatory Commission and APTEL cannot be reopened in an appeal under Section 125.

rules.reference: Electricity Act, 2003
rules.relevance: Defines 'distribution licensee'. The court used this to interpret that a licensee must operate a distribution system to supply power to consumers.

rules.reference: Special Economic Zones Act, 2005
rules.relevance: Empowers the Central Government to modify other enactments for SEZs. The court considered the scope of the notification issued under this section.

rules.case_name: Dharamvir Singh v. Union of India

rules.reference: General Rules of Guide to Medical Officers (Military Pensions), 2002

rules.case_name: Union of India v. Rajbir Singh

rules.case_name: Dharampal Satyapal Ltd. v. Deputy Commissioner of Central Excise, Gauhati and Others

rules.reference: Central Civil Services (Classification, Control and Appeal) Rules, 1965

rules.case_name: State of U.P. v. Sudhir Kumar Singh and Others

rules.reference: National Seeds Corporation Ltd. v. K.V. Rama Reddy
rules.relevance: Relied on alongside Crescent Dyes to support the principle that the right to representation depends on governing rules and is not an inherent element of natural justice.

rules.case_name: Ram Chand and Others v. Union of India and Others
rules.reference: Ram Chand and Others v. Union of India and Others
rules.relevance: Cited for the principle that a statutory authority failing to perform its duty within a reasonable time cannot take the plea of laches or delay against the litigant.

rules.case_name: Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation

rules.relevance: Holds that a 1/3rd deduction for personal expenses is appropriate for a bachelor if he has a large family dependent on his income.

rules.case_name: National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi

rules.relevance: Held that loss of future prospects is a factor for determining compensation under pecuniary loss, specifically adding 40% for deceased persons below 40 years of age, even when income is notional.

rules.provision: Regulation 33(10) and Clauses 1.11 and 1.15 of Appendix-IV

rules.relevance: Prescribes a uniform 60-day limitation period for appeals under Section 37 of the Arbitration Act for commercial disputes of specified value.

rules.case_name: N.V. International v. State of Assam
rules.reference: N.V. International v. State of Assam
rules.relevance: The court overruled this judgment, holding that it wrongly imposed a hard cap on condonation of delay for Section 37 appeals by analogy to Section 34(3), which constitutes judicial legislation.

rules.case_name: The East India Hotels Ltd. v. Smt. Mahendra Kumari and another
rules.reference: The East India Hotels Ltd. v. Smt. Mahendra Kumari and another
rules.relevance: Supported the view that when a respondent participates in the admission stage, the limitation period starts from the date of admission.

rules.reference: Civil Procedure Code, 1908
rules.relevance: Defines the admission stage hearing where the court applies its mind to the merits, relevant for determining when 'hearing' commences.

rules.case_name: Govindaraju v. Mariamman
rules.reference: Govindaraju v. Mariamman
rules.relevance: Holds that a High Court cannot set aside findings of fact recorded by the first appellate court on re-appreciation of evidence unless such findings are perverse.

rules.reference: Self-acquired property rights
rules.relevance: A coparcener has the absolute right to dispose of his self-acquired property by sale, gift, or will, distinguishing it from joint family property which cannot be disposed of by gift of undivided interest.

rules.case_name: Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari (Deceased) By LR.s.
rules.reference: Santosh Hazari v. Purushottam Tiwari (Deceased) By LR.s.
rules.relevance: Establishes that the scope of hearing a second appeal is circumscribed by the substantial questions of law formulated by the High Court.

rules.reference: Perversity in factual findings
rules.relevance: Findings based on conjectures, surmises, or ignoring relevant evidence are perverse and constitute a substantial question of law.

rules.reference: Civil Procedure Code, 1908
rules.relevance: Section 100 mandates that a second appeal can only be entertained if the case involves a substantial question of law. The High Court must formulate such a question before interfering with findings of fact.

rules.case_name: Sanjay Dhar v. J & K Public Service Commission & Anr.
rules.reference: Sanjay Dhar v. J & K Public Service Commission
rules.relevance: Established that a candidate wrongfully excluded from appointment is entitled to notional seniority from the date they should have been appointed.

rules.case_name: P. K. Haneefa v. State of Kerala
rules.reference: P. K. Haneefa v. State of Kerala
rules.relevance: Held that Rule 2(b) creates a mandatory quota for direct recruitment and consequently a quota for in-service candidates; appointments in excess of quota do not confer superior seniority.

rules.reference: Kerala State Higher Judicial Services Special Rules, 1961
rules.relevance: Establishes that one-third of permanent posts are reserved for direct recruitment, implying a corresponding two-thirds quota for appointment by transfer/promotion.

rules.reference: Notional Seniority
rules.relevance: A candidate excluded due to illegal administrative action is entitled to notional seniority from the date of appointment of peers in the same selection process.

rules.reference: Kerala State Higher Judicial Services Special Rules, 1961
rules.relevance: Provides that seniority is determined by the date of first appointment, and for simultaneous appointments, by the serial order in the appointment order.

rules.case_name: Ratna Commercial Enterprises Ltd. v. Vasutech Ltd.
rules.reference: Ratna Commercial Enterprises Ltd. v. Vasutech Ltd.
rules.relevance: Cited for the principle that a suit to restrain criminal proceedings is not maintainable under Section 41(d) of the SR Act.

rules.case_name: Cotton Corporation of India Ltd. v. United Industrial Bank Ltd.
rules.reference: Cotton Corporation of India Ltd. v. United Industrial Bank Ltd.
rules.relevance: Cited for the equitable principle that courts should not impede access to justice, supporting Section 41(b) of the SR Act.

rules.case_name: Pandurang Dhondi Chougule v. Maruti Hari Jadhav
rules.reference: Pandurang Dhondi Chougule v. Maruti Hari Jadhav
rules.relevance: Cited for the principle that revisional jurisdiction under Section 115 CPC is limited to correcting jurisdictional errors.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Orissa Amendment)
rules.relevance: The court interpreted the second proviso to Section 115 of the CPC (Orissa Amendment) to determine if the Revisional Court could vary an order to finally dispose of the suit.

rules.reference: Specific Relief Act, 1963
rules.relevance: The court held that the suit was barred as it effectively sought to restrain criminal proceedings and access to justice, which is prohibited under these sections.

rules.case_name: Secretary, Department of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pension & Anr. Vs. T. V.L.N. Mallikarjuna Rao
rules.reference: Secretary, Department of Personnel, Public Grievances & Pension & Anr. Vs. T. V.L.N. Mallikarjuna Rao
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to interpret the 1989 Office Memorandum, confirming that employees covered under it are entitled to re-fixation of pay in the respective rationalized scales with effect from their initial date of appointment.

rules.reference: Office Memorandum No. F.7(1)/IC/86(44) dated 11th September, 1989
rules.relevance: This memorandum rationalized pay scales for Electronic Data Processing posts, designating Junior Machine Operators as Data Entry Operator Grade 'A' with a pay scale of Rs.1150-1500 and stipulating that pay of existing incumbents be fixed as per Fundamental Rule 23 read with FR 22(a)(ii) when pay scales change.

rules.reference: Fundamental Rule 23 read with FR 22(a)(ii)
rules.relevance: Referenced in the Office Memorandum to determine the method for fixing the pay of existing incumbents when the pay scale of their post undergoes a change.

rules.reference: Electronic Data Processing Discipline (Group C Technical Posts) Recruitment Rules, 1992
rules.relevance: Noted by the court as part of the regulatory framework governing the recruitment and pay scales of EDP posts, issued under Article 309 of the Constitution.

rules.reference: Railway Services (Pension) Rules, 1993
rules.relevance: The court considered the respondent's argument that this rule treats contractual service followed by appointment to a substantive post as permanent service for pension calculation.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Ownership Flats (Regulation of the Promotion of Construction, Sale, Management and Transfer) Act, 1963
rules.relevance: Impose obligations on the promoter to form a cooperative society and convey the title to the society within prescribed periods.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Ownership Flats (Regulation of the Promotion of Construction, Sale, Management and Transfer) Act, 1963
rules.relevance: Exempts promoters from obtaining consent for the construction of additional buildings or structures under a scheme or project of development in the layout plan, provided the plan is approved by the competent authority.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Ownership Flats (Regulation of the Promotion of Construction, etc.) Rules, 1964
rules.relevance: Statutory clauses requiring full disclosure of FSI and stating that residual FSI is available to the promoter until society registration, after which it belongs to the society.

rules.case_name: Ravindra Mutneja and Ors. v. Bhavan Corporation and Ors.
rules.reference: Ravindra Mutneja and Ors. v. Bhavan Corporation and Ors.
rules.relevance: Held that if a building is put up as a wing of an existing building, it cannot be constructed without prior permission of flat takers, distinguishing it from additional buildings under a scheme.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Ownership Flats (Regulation of the Promotion of Construction, Sale, Management and Transfer) Act, 1963
rules.relevance: Prohibits promoters from making alterations or additions to the structure of the building without the previous consent of all flat takers, unless exempted by Section 7A.

rules.reference: Central Excise Act, 1944
rules.relevance: Establishes that any person aggrieved by an order of the Commissioner (A) is entitled to appeal to the Tribunal, and the Commissioner's order is treated as an order of an adjudicating authority.

rules.reference: Entitlement to MODVAT credit
rules.relevance: Even if bought-out items are dutiable, the assessee is entitled to the benefit of MODVAT credit, which must be considered in quantifying the net duty liability.

rules.reference: Central Excise Act, 1944
rules.relevance: Discussed to highlight that the power of remand by the Commissioner (A) was withdrawn by amendment, reinforcing that the Commissioner exercises adjudicating powers and their orders are appealable.

rules.reference: Excisability is a matter of principle
rules.relevance: The Tribunal is the highest authority to decide on facts whether items are dutiable and is not bound by the Commissioner's earlier decision on the question of dutiability.

rules.reference: Central Excise & Salt Act, 1944
rules.relevance: The court considered this provision to determine if the extended limitation period applied due to the wilful suppression of material facts by the assessee.

rules.case_name: State of A.P. v. Bimal Krishna Kundu
rules.reference: State of A.P. v. Bimal Krishna Kundu
rules.relevance: Supports the view that granting anticipatory bail in cases of well-orchestrated conspiracy or serious allegations can harm the investigation and public interest.

rules.case_name: State Rep. By The CBI v. Anil Sharma
rules.reference: State Rep. By The CBI v. Anil Sharma
rules.relevance: Held that custodial interrogation is more effective than questioning a suspect protected by anticipatory bail.

rules.case_name: Ravindra Saxena v. State of Rajasthan
rules.reference: Ravindra Saxena v. State of Rajasthan
rules.relevance: Distinguished because it involved a civil/commercial dispute, whereas the present case involves serious allegations of corruption and misappropriation of public funds.

rules.case_name: Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar and another
rules.reference: Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: Held that anticipatory bail in serious offences can be granted only in exceptional circumstances.

rules.case_name: Bhadresh Bipinbhai Sheth v. State of Gujarat
rules.reference: Bhadresh Bipinbhai Sheth v. State of Gujarat
rules.relevance: Confirms that the court granting bail has the power to cancel it based on new material or circumstances, and no inflexible guidelines exist for such decisions.

rules.case_name: Vaddeboyina Tulasamma v. Vaddeboyina Sesha Reddy
rules.reference: Vaddeboyina Tulasamma v. Vaddeboyina Sesha Reddy
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to establish that Section 14(2) applies only when property is acquired for the first time under a decree or instrument prescribing a restricted estate, without any pre-existing right such as maintenance.

rules.reference: Burden of Proof in Joint Family Property Claims
rules.relevance: The initial burden is on the party claiming joint family property to prove the existence of a nucleus and that the property was acquired from joint family funds. Only upon discharge of this burden does it shift to the other party.

rules.case_name: Chandramohan Ramchandra Patil and Others v. Bapu Koyappa Patil (Dead) Through LRs and Others
rules.reference: Chandramohan Ramchandra Patil and Others v. Bapu Koyappa Patil (Dead) Through LRs and Others
rules.relevance: Holds that an appellate court can grant relief to non-appealing plaintiffs and make adverse orders against defendants under Order 41 Rules 4 and 33 CPC.

rules.case_name: Bhagwan Swaroop and Others v. Mool Chand and Others
rules.reference: Bhagwan Swaroop and Others v. Mool Chand and Others
rules.relevance: Establishes that in a partition suit, the positions of plaintiff and defendant are interchangeable.

rules.case_name: Appasaheb Chamdgade v. Devendra Chamdgade and Ors.
rules.reference: Appasaheb Chamdgade v. Devendra Chamdgade and Ors.
rules.relevance: Affirms that there is no presumption of joint family property; the burden lies on the person claiming joint family status to prove acquisition from joint family funds.

rules.reference: Waqf Act, 1995
rules.relevance: The court interpreted this provision to determine that Senior Advocates nominated in the absence of Muslim Bar Council members are 'nominated' members, not 'elected' members.

rules.case_name: M.H. Jawahirullah and others vs. Government of Tamil Nadu and others
rules.reference: M.H. Jawahirullah and others vs. Government of Tamil Nadu and others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to affirm the legislative intent of democratic administration in the Waqf Board, preventing arbitrary nomination by the State.

rules.reference: Waqf Act, 1995
rules.relevance: The court noted this as the specific exception allowing nomination when an electoral college is not practicable, which overrides Section 14(4). The State failed to use this provision.

rules.reference: Waqf Act, 1995
rules.relevance: This section mandates that the number of elected members must always be more than nominated members. The court held that ensuring this composition is the duty of the State Government.

rules.reference: Waqf Act, 1995
rules.relevance: The court held that the power to supersede under Section 99(1) is restricted by the second proviso, which requires prima facie evidence of financial irregularity, misconduct, or violation of the Act by the Board.

rules.case_name: Mohd. Azad alias Samin v. State of West Bengal
rules.reference: Mohd. Azad alias Samin v. State of West Bengal
rules.relevance: Defines the 'last seen theory', requiring a small time gap between seeing the accused and deceased alive and finding the body dead.

rules.case_name: Sahadevan v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: Sahadevan v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.relevance: Laid down that extra-judicial confession is weak evidence and must be examined with care, but gains credibility if supported by a chain of cogent circumstances.

rules.case_name: State Rep. by Inspector of Police v. Saravanan
rules.reference: State Rep. by Inspector of Police v. Saravanan
rules.relevance: Held that minor contradictions, omissions, or improvements in witness testimony do not vitiate the evidence unless they materially affect the core of the prosecution case.

rules.case_name: John Pandian v. State Represented by Inspector of Police, Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: John Pandian v. State Represented by Inspector of Police, Tamil Nadu
rules.relevance: Supported the view that recovery of a weapon stained with human blood aids the prosecution case if the accused offers no explanation for the presence of blood.

rules.case_name: Padala Veera Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh
rules.reference: Padala Veera Reddy v. State of Andhra Pradesh
rules.relevance: Established tests for circumstantial evidence, including that circumstances must be cogently established and form a complete chain excluding other hypotheses.

rules.case_name: Indian Oil Corpn. v NEPC India Ltd. & Ors.
rules.reference: Indian Oil Corpn. v NEPC India Ltd. & Ors.
rules.relevance: Guiding principles for exercising Section 482 powers, emphasizing that civil disputes should not be converted into criminal cases to apply pressure.

rules.case_name: Union of India & Ors. Vs. Cipla Ltd. & Anr.
rules.reference: Union of India & Ors. Vs. Cipla Ltd. & Anr.
rules.relevance: Defined forum shopping and established a functional test to determine if a litigant is creating circumstances to confer jurisdiction for a favorable outcome.

rules.case_name: Randheer Singh v. The State of U.P. & others
rules.reference: Randheer Singh v. The State of U.P. & others
rules.relevance: Cited to support the principle that purely civil disputes involving financial transactions should not be given the color of criminal cases.

rules.case_name: Usha Chakraborty & Anr. v. State of West Bengal & Anr.
rules.reference: Usha Chakraborty & Anr. v. State of West Bengal & Anr.
rules.relevance: Held that disputes essentially of a civil nature given a cloak of a criminal offence can be quashed under Section 482 CrPC.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The sections under which the FIR was registered; the court examined whether the facts disclosed a prima facie case for cheating, forgery, and criminal conspiracy.

rules.case_name: Commissioner of Central Excise, Delhi v. Maruti Udyog Limited
rules.reference: Commissioner of Central Excise, Delhi v. Maruti Udyog Limited
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to affirm the principle that when a cum-duty price is charged, the element of excise duty must be excluded from the sale price to determine the assessable value.

rules.case_name: SACI Allied Products Ltd., U.P. v. Commissioner of Central Excise, Meerut
rules.reference: SACI Allied Products Ltd., U.P. v. Commissioner of Central Excise, Meerut
rules.relevance: Holds that when sales are made to both independent and related parties, the price charged to independent buyers should be adopted as the basis for excise duty on related sales.

rules.case_name: Asstt. Collector of Central Excise v. Bata India Limited
rules.reference: Asstt. Collector of Central Excise v. Bata India Limited
rules.relevance: The court referred to this judgment, as cited in Maruti Udyog, to support the interpretation of Section 4(4)(d)(ii) regarding the exclusion of duty from the wholesale price.

rules.reference: Notification No. 175/86-CE
rules.relevance: The court examined this notification to establish that the assessee was not eligible for exemption because the brand name belonged to another manufacturer not entitled to small-scale exemption.

rules.case_name: Continental Foundation Jt. Venture v. Commissioner of Central Excise
rules.reference: Continental Foundation Jt. Venture v. Commissioner of Central Excise
rules.relevance: Relied upon to reiterate that suppression means failure to disclose full information with intent to evade duty, and mere omission is not suppression.

rules.case_name: Bank of India v. Ketan Parekh
rules.reference: Bank of India v. Ketan Parekh
rules.relevance: Established the principle that when two special acts have non-obstante clauses, they must be harmonized based on their dominant purpose rather than one simply overriding the other.

rules.reference: Presumption of love and affection
rules.relevance: The court noted that transfers by senior citizens to family members are often made out of love and affection without an expectation of return; therefore, the existence of a condition of care must be specifically established and cannot be presumed.

rules.reference: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
rules.relevance: This section empowers the Tribunal to declare a transfer of property void if it was made subject to the condition that the transferee provide basic amenities and physical needs, and the transferee fails to do so. The court analyzed whether these specific conditions were met.

rules.reference: Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007
rules.relevance: Deals with the enforcement of maintenance rights against transferees. The court interpreted this to determine if it implicitly grants power to evict a daughter-in-law from a shared household.

rules.case_name: Satish Chandra Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja
rules.reference: Satish Chandra Ahuja v. Sneha Ahuja
rules.relevance: Confirmed that 'shared household' under the PWDV Act includes households belonging to the joint family of the respondent, irrespective of the aggrieved person's title or interest.

rules.reference: Irrelevance of complainant's credibility at initial stage
rules.relevance: The court held that the credibility of the complainant and allegations of malafides are not relevant grounds for quashing proceedings at the initial stage.

rules.case_name: Vesa Holdings (P) Ltd. and Anr. v. State of Kerala and Ors.
rules.reference: Vesa Holdings (P) Ltd. and Anr. v. State of Kerala and Ors.
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this precedent, clarifying that while breach of contract does not always amount to cheating, the presence of deception at the inception (as alleged here via forgery) makes it a criminal offence.

rules.case_name: Shiv Shankar Singh v. State of Bihar and Anr.
rules.reference: Shiv Shankar Singh v. State of Bihar and Anr.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to hold that there is no statutory bar against filing a second complaint on the same facts if the earlier complaint was not disposed of on merits.

rules.reference: Non-bailable warrants
rules.relevance: Non-bailable warrants should not be issued routinely and only when necessary to prevent evasion of law or tampering with evidence.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The sections under which the FIR was registered; the court examined whether the facts disclosed a prima facie case for cheating, forgery, and criminal conspiracy.

rules.case_name: Durga Prasanna Tripathy v. Arundhati Tripathy
rules.reference: Durga Prasanna Tripathy v. Arundhati Tripathy
rules.relevance: Cited as authority for affirming divorce and directing alimony under Article 142 due to irretrievable breakdown.

rules.case_name: Swati Verma v. Rajan Verma
rules.reference: Swati Verma v. Rajan Verma
rules.relevance: Cited as authority for exercising Article 142 to grant divorce due to irretrievable breakdown of marriage.

rules.reference: Hindu Marriage Act, 1955
rules.relevance: Defines statutory grounds for divorce (cruelty and desertion) which the appellant failed to prove, necessitating the invocation of Article 142.

rules.case_name: Ramesh Chander v. Savitri
rules.reference: Ramesh Chander v. Savitri
rules.relevance: Established the principle that when a marriage is dead emotionally and practically, its continuance amounts to cruelty, justifying dissolution under Article 142.

rules.case_name: Vishnu Dutt Sharma vs. Manju Sharma
rules.reference: Vishnu Dutt Sharma vs. Manju Sharma
rules.relevance: Held that irretrievable breakdown of marriage is not a ground for divorce under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

rules.case_name: Anokhilal vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.reference: Anokhilal vs. State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to set aside the conviction, noting that the legal aid counsel was not given sufficient time to prepare, and to lay down norms for appointing senior counsel in death penalty cases.

rules.case_name: Bashira vs. State of U.P.
rules.reference: Bashira vs. State of U.P.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to establish that a trial conducted in a hurried manner without sufficient time for the defense counsel violates the procedure established by law and renders the conviction void.

rules.case_name: Rahul v. State of Delhi, Ministry of Home Affairs & Anr.
rules.reference: Rahul v. State of Delhi, Ministry of Home Affairs & Anr.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to highlight that DNA evidence must be scientifically and legally proved, and that mere exhibition of reports without examining experts or establishing chain of custody is insufficient.

rules.reference: Right to Fair Trial and Judicial Calm
rules.relevance: The court held that a hasty trial depriving the accused of adequate time to prepare a defense violates the principle of fair trial and judicial calm, necessitating a de novo trial.

rules.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
rules.relevance: These sections mandate that the High Court must independently examine the entire evidence in death reference cases and may direct further inquiry or acquit the accused if the conviction is not justified.

rules.reference: West Bengal Land Reforms and Tenancy Tribunal Act, 1997
rules.relevance: This provision governed the appeal filed by Respondents 1 and 2 to the High Court against the Tribunal's order.

rules.reference: West Bengal Estate Acquisition Act, 1953
rules.relevance: The court reviewed the history of proceedings under this section to understand the background of the dispute and the validity of the initial cancellation orders.

rules.reference: The Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceiling on Holdings) Act, 1961
rules.relevance: The court held that the Collector's jurisdiction under this section is limited to calculating ceiling area and delimiting surplus land. It does not extend to conducting an enquiry to declare a pre-cut-off partition deed as sham or void.

rules.reference: The Maharashtra Agricultural Lands (Ceiling on Holdings) Act, 1961
rules.relevance: The exclusion of pleaders from proceedings under the Act indicates that the Collector's role is administrative and limited, not judicial. This supports the view that the Collector cannot conduct complex trials to declare deeds void.

rules.reference: Jurisdiction of Revenue Authorities vs. Civil Courts
rules.relevance: The court held that declaring a partition deed sham or void is a matter for a Civil Court, not the Collector under the 1961 Act, especially for deeds executed before the cut-off date.

rules.case_name: Goutam Kundu vs. State of West Bengal
rules.reference: Goutam Kundu vs. State of West Bengal
rules.relevance: Held that courts cannot order blood/DNA tests as a matter of course; there must be a strong prima facie case of non-access, and no one can be compelled to give a blood sample.

rules.reference: Test of 'eminent need' for DNA testing
rules.relevance: DNA tests should only be ordered if there is an 'eminent need' and it is not possible to reach the truth without such a test, considering the potential to bastardize a child.

rules.case_name: Gautam Kundu v. State of West Bengal
rules.reference: Gautam Kundu v. State of West Bengal
rules.relevance: Establishes that courts cannot order blood/DNA tests as a matter of course, no one can be compelled to give a blood sample, and there must be a strong prima facie case of non-access.

rules.reference: Convention on the Rights of the Child
rules.relevance: Reinforces the child's right to identity, protection from violence/abuse, and the principle that the best interests of the child are a primary consideration.

rules.case_name: Dipanwita Roy vs. Ronobroto Roy
rules.reference: Dipanwita Roy vs. Ronobroto Roy
rules.relevance: Distinguished because the husband in that case pleaded non-access, whereas in the present case, access was admitted, making the DNA test unnecessary and the presumption irrebuttable.

rules.case_name: State of Kerala v. Puttamana Ilath Jathavedan Namboodiri
rules.reference: State of Kerala v. Puttamana Ilath Jathavedan Namboodiri
rules.relevance: Clarified that revisional jurisdiction is supervisory and not appellate; re-appreciation of evidence is inappropriate unless there is a glaring feature amounting to gross miscarriage of justice.

rules.reference: Fraud on Court
rules.relevance: A litigant who suppresses material facts or withholds vital documents to gain an advantage commits fraud on the court and is disentitled from relief.

rules.case_name: Karamjit Singh v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Karamjit Singh v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: Established that relief under the Probation of Offenders Act should be granted only in offences not of a very grave nature or where mens rea is absent.

rules.case_name: Superintendent, Central Excise, Bangalore v. Ballubali
rules.reference: Superintendent, Central Excise, Bangalore v. Ballubali
rules.relevance: Held that provisions prescribing minimum sentences are inconsistent with the PO Act and must yield to the specific statute if it bars discretion.

rules.reference: Definition of Mandatory Minimum Sentence
rules.relevance: A mandatory minimum sentence leaves no discretion to the court; if a statute allows reduction of sentence for special reasons, it does not constitute a mandatory minimum that bars probation.

rules.reference: Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
rules.relevance: Requires prior approval for investigation of public servants, but the first proviso exempts cases involving arrest on the spot for accepting undue advantage.

rules.reference: Balance between liberty and investigation
rules.relevance: Courts must balance the liberty of the individual under Article 21 with the need for a fair and free investigation.

rules.case_name: Shri Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and others v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Shri Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and others v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: Established that anticipatory bail cannot be sought after arrest, rendering the SLP in the CBI case infructuous.

rules.case_name: Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar and another
rules.reference: Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: Held that anticipatory bail in serious offences can be granted only in exceptional circumstances.

rules.case_name: State Rep. By The CBI v. Anil Sharma
rules.reference: State Rep. By The CBI v. Anil Sharma
rules.relevance: Held that custodial interrogation is more effective than questioning a suspect protected by anticipatory bail.

rules.reference: Disputed questions of fact in writ proceedings
rules.relevance: The principle that High Courts should decline to try writ petitions raising complex questions of fact requiring oral evidence, relegating parties to normal remedies like civil suits.

rules.case_name: Gunwant Kaur v. Municipal Committee
rules.reference: Gunwant Kaur v. Municipal Committee
rules.relevance: Clarified that while the existence of factual questions does not automatically oust jurisdiction, the High Court must exercise discretion to determine if the matter is suitable for writ proceedings.

rules.case_name: Union of India v. T.R. Verma
rules.reference: Union of India v. T.R. Verma
rules.relevance: Held that serious disputes of fact that cannot be satisfactorily decided without taking evidence should not be decided in writ proceedings.

rules.case_name: Mahanta Moti Das v. SP. Sahid
rules.reference: Mahanta Moti Das v. SP. Sahid
rules.relevance: Established that High Courts should not entertain petitions involving complicated facts that require investigation and recording of evidence.

rules.case_name: Gajraj and others vs. State of U.P. and others
rules.reference: Gajraj and others vs. State of U.P. and others
rules.relevance: Established the principle that where acquisition proceedings are flawed but third-party rights have accrued, equities are balanced by paying additional compensation rather than quashing the acquisition.

rules.reference: Suo Motu Writ Petition (Civil) No. 3 of 2020
rules.relevance: Directed that the period from 15.03.2020 to 02.10.2021 shall be excluded in computing the period of limitation for any suit, appeal, application, or proceeding.

rules.case_name: SS Group Pvt. Ltd. v. Aaditiya J. Garg
rules.reference: SS Group Pvt. Ltd. v. Aaditiya J. Garg
rules.relevance: Held that the limitation for filing a written statement is deemed extended under the orders passed in SMWP No. 3 of 2020.

rules.provision: Order V Rule 1(1) (as amended by Commercial Courts Act, 2015)
rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: Amends the summons provision to include the 120-day forfeiture rule for written statements in commercial suits.

rules.case_name: Sagufa Ahmed v. Upper Assam Polywood Products Private Limited
rules.reference: Sagufa Ahmed v. Upper Assam Polywood Products Private Limited
rules.relevance: Distinguished because it was decided before the final orders in SMWP No. 3 of 2020 which explicitly excluded the pandemic period for computing limitation.

rules.case_name: SCG Contracts (India) Private Limited v. K.S. Chamankar Infrastructure Private Limited
rules.reference: SCG Contracts (India) Private Limited v. K.S. Chamankar Infrastructure Private Limited
rules.relevance: Established the strict mandatory nature of the 120-day limit in normal circumstances, but distinguished here due to extraordinary pandemic conditions.

rules.case_name: Jodhpur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and another vs Nanu Ram and others
rules.reference: Jodhpur Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd. and another vs Nanu Ram and others
rules.relevance: The court referred to this decision to understand that mere completion of two years is not the only criterion for regularization and that grant of pay scale is distinct from grant of permanency.

rules.case_name: Indu Shekhar Singh v. State of U.P.
rules.reference: Indu Shekhar Singh v. State of U.P.
rules.relevance: Held that a High Court cannot determine inter se seniority in the absence of necessary parties who were not joined in the writ petition.

rules.reference: GO Ms No 1499, Labour and Employment (Q1) Department
