rules.relevance: Held that Rule 2(b) creates a mandatory quota for direct recruitment and consequently a quota for in-service candidates; appointments in excess of quota do not confer superior seniority.

rules.case_name: B.S. Yadav & Ors. v. State of Haryana & Ors.
rules.reference: B.S. Yadav & Ors. v. State of Haryana & Ors.
rules.relevance: The court relied on this to establish that the rule-making function under Article 309 is legislative, preventing the selection committee from legislating selection rules.

rules.case_name: Pervez Qadir v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.reference: Pervez Qadir v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this case, noting that while character rolls might suffice for transition between similar services, they are insufficient for appointment to a new service like teaching.

rules.reference: Jammu & Kashmir Medical Education (Gazetted) Service Recruitment Rules, 1979
rules.relevance: Establishes that the Directorate of Medical Education does not have a cadre of Assistant Surgeons, confirming that posting there was outside the appellants' substantive cadre.

rules.reference: Import Export Policy for April 1990-March 1993 (New Policy)

rules.reference: REP Circular No. 11/93 dated 5th May, 1993
rules.relevance: Mandated payment of a 20% premium instead of issuing licences for pending applications regarding exports prior to March 1, 1992, provided the applicant was eligible.

rules.reference: Import Export Policy for April 1988-March 1991 (Old Policy)
rules.relevance: Established that Trading Houses were eligible for additional licences based on admissible exports made in the preceding licensing year.

rules.case_name: Swastika Enterprises Vs. Commissioner of Customs, Kolkata
rules.reference: Swastika Enterprises Vs. Commissioner of Customs, Kolkata
rules.relevance: Held that an endorsement on a Bill of Entry constitutes a 'notice of demand' for the purposes of the KVSS, and that the term 'determined as due or payable' should be widely interpreted.

rules.reference: Foreign Trade Policy, 2004-2009
rules.relevance: States that exports permitted under the policy will ordinarily be permitted notwithstanding subsequent restrictions if shipment is made within the validity of an irrevocable letter of credit established before the restriction.

rules.case_name: Thamma Venkata Subbamma (dead) by Lrs. V Thamma Rattamma and Others
rules.reference: Thamma Venkata Subbamma (dead) by Lrs. V Thamma Rattamma and Others
rules.relevance: Establishes that a gift by a coparcener of his undivided interest in coparcenary property is void ab initio.

rules.case_name: Madhukar Vishwanath Vs. Madahav and Others
rules.reference: Madhukar Vishwanath Vs. Madahav and Others
rules.relevance: Established that Article 60, not Article 65, applies to suits seeking to set aside transfers by guardians.

rules.reference: Hindu Minority and Guardianship Act, 1956
rules.relevance: Prohibits a natural guardian from transferring immovable property of a minor without prior court permission.

rules.case_name: Vishwambhar and Others Vs. Laxminarayan (Dead) Through LRs. and Another
rules.reference: Vishwambhar and Others Vs. Laxminarayan (Dead) Through LRs. and Another
rules.relevance: Held that a suit for possession without a prayer to set aside voidable sale deeds is not maintainable.

rules.reference: Distinction between Void and Voidable
rules.relevance: Voidable agreements are valid until annulled and require specific legal action to be set aside, unlike void acts which can be ignored.

rules.case_name: Ravinder Singh v. State of Haryana
rules.reference: Ravinder Singh v. State of Haryana
rules.relevance: Held that a reasonable proportion must be maintained between the seriousness of the crime and the punishment.

rules.case_name: State of Punjab v. Bawa Singh

rules.relevance: Held that undue sympathy leading to inadequate sentences undermines public confidence and that sentences must be commensurate with the gravity of the offence.

rules.reference: Deterrence and Social Protection
rules.relevance: Sentencing must protect society and stamp out criminal proclivity, reflecting public abhorrence of the crime and preventing lawlessness.

rules.reference: Delay in Proceedings as Ground for Leniency
rules.relevance: Delay in trial or lapse of time is not a valid ground for reducing sentence to the period undergone if it shocks the conscience of society or undermines deterrence.

rules.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
rules.relevance: Grants courts the power to alter charges to ensure justice is not defeated by technicalities, provided no prejudice is caused to the accused.

rules.case_name: Fatindra Nath Gupta v. The Province of Bihar and Others
rules.reference: Fatindra Nath Gupta v. The Province of Bihar and Others
rules.relevance: Distinguished on the ground that the present case involved no delegation of legislative power, as the Legislature itself fixed the duration of the Act.

rules.reference: Essential Supplies (Temporary Powers) Act, 1946
rules.relevance: Provides that the Act ceases to have effect on the expiration of the period mentioned in Section 4 of the India (Central Government and Legislature) Act, 1946.

rules.reference: Mens rea inference
rules.relevance: Criminal intent can be inferred from facts such as false statements regarding the nature of goods and inability to produce required permits.

rules.reference: India (Central Government and Legislature) Act, 1946
rules.relevance: Defines the period of operation of the Essential Supplies Act, allowing for extensions up to five years by legislative resolution.

rules.reference: Indian Independence Act, 1947
rules.relevance: Authorized adaptations substituting the Constituent Assembly for Parliament, validating the resolutions extending the Essential Supplies Act.

rules.reference: Welfare of the child as paramount consideration

rules.reference: Contempt of Courts Act, 1971

rules.reference: Standard for civil contempt proceedings involving mutual obligations
rules.relevance: The court emphasized that in contempt proceedings based on breach of consent terms, the court must first determine which party failed to fulfill their obligations before punishing the other.

rules.reference: Juvenile Justice (Care & Protection) Act, 2015
rules.relevance: Defines 'best interest of the child' as the basis for decisions regarding the child's welfare.

rules.case_name: A Shanker v. State of Karnataka
rules.reference: A Shanker v. State of Karnataka
rules.relevance: Cited to support the principle that normal discrepancies due to errors of observation or memory do not render evidence unreliable if they do not affect the core of the case.

rules.reference: Minor discrepancies in witness testimony
rules.relevance: The court held that minor contradictions or embellishments on trivial matters do not affect the core of the prosecution case and should not lead to rejection of evidence.

rules.case_name: Gulab Chand v. State of MP
rules.reference: Gulab Chand v. State of MP
rules.relevance: Held that recent possession of stolen articles, considering the 'important time factor', allows a presumption of guilt under Section 114 of the Evidence Act.

rules.reference: Failure to cross-examine on material issues
rules.relevance: The court held that if a question is not put to a witness in cross-examination who could furnish an explanation, the correctness or legality of that fact/issue cannot be raised later.

rules.reference: Doctrine of Confirmation by Subsequent Events
rules.relevance: Underpins Section 27 of the Evidence Act, establishing that discovery of a fact based on information from an accused guarantees the truth of that information.

rules.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973

rules.case_name: Bharat Damodar Kale & Anr. v. State of A.P.

rules.relevance: Established that the date of filing the complaint is the crucial date for computing limitation, not the date of taking cognizance.

rules.reference: Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
rules.relevance: Provides for exclusion of time during diligent prosecution, indicating that the limitation scheme governs the prosecution's actions rather than the court's internal processing time.

rules.reference: Criminal Procedure Code, 1973
rules.relevance: This section prescribes the period of limitation for taking cognizance of offences. The central issue is determining the relevant date for computing this period.

rules.case_name: Kamal Javeri & Anr. v. Chandulal Gulabchand Kothari & Anr.
rules.reference: Kamal Javeri & Anr. v. Chandulal Gulabchand Kothari & Anr.
rules.relevance: Supported the view that limitation is related to the filing of the complaint, preventing illogical results where complainants are penalized for court delays.

rules.case_name: Ramashish Yadav v. State of Bihar
rules.reference: Ramashish Yadav v. State of Bihar
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to establish that common intention developing on the spot must be the result of prior concert.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The court upheld the conviction under this section, which applies when the act is done with knowledge that it is likely to cause death, but without intention to cause death.

rules.case_name: State of Gujarat v. Bai Fatima
rules.reference: State of Gujarat v. Bai Fatima
rules.relevance: Establishes that non-explanation of minor and superficial injuries does not affect the prosecution case if the evidence is clear, cogent, and outweighs the omission.

rules.reference: Distinction between intention to cause death and knowledge that act is likely to cause death

rules.case_name: Deo Narain v. The State of U.P.

rules.relevance: Held that the right of private defence is preventive and one cannot be expected to coolly determine the precise severity of blow required in moments of excitement.

rules.case_name: Abdul Rahim & Ors. v. Tufan Gazi and Ors.

rules.relevance: The court used this precedent to affirm that specific performance cannot be granted to a party who has not been ready and willing to perform the contract at all stages.

rules.case_name: Abdul Haq v. Mohammad Yehia Khan

rules.case_name: Dilbagrai Punjabi vs. Sharad Chandra

rules.case_name: Union of India v. G Hassan Ali Khan

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860

rules.case_name: State of UP v. Hari Ram
rules.reference: State of UP v. Hari Ram
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment for the interpretation that vesting under Section 10(3) is de jure and does not imply de facto possession, and that notice under Section 10(5) is mandatory.

rules.case_name: Competent Authority, Calcutta, under the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976 and another v. David Mantosh and others
rules.reference: Competent Authority, Calcutta, under the Urban Land (Ceiling and Regulation) Act, 1976 and another v. David Mantosh and others
rules.relevance: The court relied on this judgment to hold that the ULC Act is a self-contained code and civil courts lack jurisdiction to declare orders passed by competent authorities as illegal or non est.

rules.case_name: State of U.P. v. Hari Ram
rules.reference: State of U.P. v. Hari Ram
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to interpret 'deemed vesting' versus 'de facto possession' under the Repeal Act, holding that actual possession is required for the saving clause to apply.

rules.reference: Securitisation and Reconstruction of Financial Assets and Enforcement of Security Interest Act, 2002
rules.relevance: Governs the issuance of demand and possession notices; the court examined whether errors in these notices vitiated the proceedings.

rules.case_name: United Bank of India vs. Satyawati Tondon & Others
rules.reference: United Bank of India vs. Satyawati Tondon & Others
rules.relevance: Established that High Courts must insist on the exhaustion of alternative statutory remedies before entertaining petitions under Article 226, especially in matters involving bank dues.

rules.reference: Inconsequential Error
rules.relevance: A typographical error in property description does not vitiate auction proceedings if it does not cause ambiguity or prejudice regarding the identity of the property.

rules.reference: Valid Tender for Redemption
rules.relevance: A tender is valid only if it complies with the terms of the loan and is made to the correct entity (the bank/loan account), not a third party or individual officer.

rules.reference: Registration Act, 1908
rules.relevance: Exempts sale certificates granted in public auction by civil or revenue officers from mandatory registration; the High Court applied this, though the Supreme Court did not finally decide the applicability to bank officers.

rules.case_name: National Thermal Power Corporation Ltd. v. Madhya Pradesh State Electricity Board
rules.reference: National Thermal Power Corporation Ltd. v. Madhya Pradesh State Electricity Board
rules.relevance: Distinguished because it involved CERC Regulations where no provision for interest existed, unlike the explicit restitutionary clause in the present PPAs.

rules.case_name: Energy Watchdog v. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
rules.reference: Energy Watchdog v. Central Electricity Regulatory Commission
rules.relevance: Affirmed that the restitutionary principle in Clause 13.2 of PPAs must be kept in mind when determining compensation for change in law.

rules.reference: Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs)
rules.relevance: Specifies that tariff adjustments for Change in Law are effective from the date of the change in law, not the date of regulatory approval.

rules.case_name: Chertsey Urban District Council v. Mixnam's Properties Ltd.
rules.reference: Chertsey Urban District Council v. Mixnam's Properties Ltd.
rules.relevance: The court referred to this House of Lords decision regarding the principle that subordinate legislation cannot be ultra vires, but found it not directly applicable to the facts.

rules.case_name: South Eastern Coalfields Ltd. v. State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.reference: South Eastern Coalfields Ltd. v. State of Madhya Pradesh
rules.relevance: Distinguished because it involved interest based on equity and statutory provisions (Sale of Goods Act), whereas the present case relies on an explicit contractual restitutionary clause.

rules.case_name: Trimukh Maruti Kirkan v. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: Trimukh Maruti Kirkan v. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: The court relied on this case for the principle that failure by a husband to explain his wife's death when they were last seen together is a strong circumstance of guilt.

rules.case_name: Satpal v. State of Haryana
rules.reference: Satpal v. State of Haryana
rules.relevance: Established that the 'last seen' theory is weak evidence by itself and requires corroboration to sustain a conviction.

rules.case_name: Asar Mohammad v. State of U.P.
rules.reference: Asar Mohammad v. State of U.P.
rules.relevance: Reiterated the legal standards for maintaining a conviction based solely on circumstantial evidence.

rules.case_name: State of U.P. v. Gambhir Singh
rules.reference: State of U.P. v. Gambhir Singh
rules.relevance: Reaffirms that if two views are reasonably possible on the same evidence, the one in favor of the accused must be preferred.

rules.case_name: Kuldip Singh v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Kuldip Singh v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this case, noting that while extra-judicial confession is weak evidence, in the present case it was corroborated by recovery of the body and identification.

rules.case_name: Church of Christ Charitable Trust and Educational Charitable Society Vs. Ponniamman Educational Trust
rules.reference: Church of Christ Charitable Trust and Educational Charitable Society Vs. Ponniamman Educational Trust
rules.relevance: Reiterated the principle that the court must scrutinize only the averments in the plaint and cannot rely on external evidence or defendant's defenses at the stage of deciding an application under Order VII Rule 11.

rules.case_name: Saleem Bhai and Others Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others
rules.reference: Saleem Bhai and Others Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others
rules.relevance: Established that for the purposes of Order VII Rule 11, only the averments in the plaint are germane; pleas taken by the defendant in the written statement are wholly irrelevant.

rules.reference: Limitation Act, 1963
rules.relevance: The court noted that determining which article applies depends on factual findings regarding the date of knowledge of the fraud, making limitation a triable issue rather than a ground for immediate rejection.

rules.provision: Form Nos. 47 and 48 of Appendix A
rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: Statutory forms for specific performance suits requiring the date of the agreement to be mentioned to show the suit is not barred by limitation.

rules.case_name: Rathnavathi & Another vs. Kavita Ganashamdas
rules.reference: Rathnavathi & Another vs. Kavita Ganashamdas
rules.relevance: Established that the bar under Order II Rule 2 is not attracted when the causes of action for injunction and specific performance are independent.

rules.reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 (as amended in 2015)
rules.relevance: Analyzed to determine that disqualification for being an employee applies only to current employees ('is an employee'), not former employees, supporting the validity of the nominee's appointment.

rules.case_name: Locabail Ltd. v. Bayfield Properties
rules.reference: Locabail Ltd. v. Bayfield Properties
rules.relevance: Holds that the greater the passage of time between the event relied on for bias and the case, the weaker the objection.

rules.case_name: SBP & Co. v. Patel Engineering Ltd. and Another
rules.reference: SBP & Co. v. Patel Engineering Ltd. and Another
rules.relevance: The court relied on this 7-Judge Bench decision to define the limited jurisdiction of the Chief Justice under Section 11(6) and to uphold the principle that an arbitration agreement can stand independent of a void main agreement.

rules.case_name: Re Medicaments and related Classes of Goods (No.2)
rules.reference: Re Medicaments and related Classes of Goods (No.2)
rules.relevance: Propounds the 'real danger' test for bias: whether a fair-minded and informed observer would conclude there was a real possibility of bias.

rules.reference: Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996
rules.relevance: The court cited this provision to affirm that a declaration that the main contract is null and void does not automatically invalidate the arbitration clause.

rules.case_name: Kalyan Chandra Sarkar v. Rajesh Ranjan @ Pappu Yadav and another
rules.reference: Kalyan Chandra Sarkar v. Rajesh Ranjan @ Pappu Yadav and another
rules.relevance: Establishes parameters for granting bail, including nature of accusation, severity of punishment, and apprehension of witness tampering.

rules.case_name: Daulat Ram and others v. State of Haryana
rules.reference: Daulat Ram and others v. State of Haryana
rules.relevance: Holds that cancellation of bail requires cogent and overwhelming circumstances or supervening events non-conducive to a fair trial.

rules.case_name: Vipin Kumar Dhir v. State of Punjab
rules.reference: Vipin Kumar Dhir v. State of Punjab
rules.relevance: Holds that bail can be revoked if the court considered irrelevant factors or ignored relevant material, rendering the order legally untenable.

rules.reference: Protection of Children from Sexual Offences Act, 2012
rules.relevance: Creates a presumption of guilt for certain offences under the Act, which the High Court failed to consider.

rules.case_name: Kanwar Singh Meena v. State of Rajasthan & Anr.
rules.reference: Kanwar Singh Meena v. State of Rajasthan & Anr.
rules.relevance: Holds that bail can be cancelled if the order suffers from serious infirmities, ignores relevant material, or takes into account irrelevant material.

rules.case_name: Meena (Smt) w/o Balwant Hemke vs. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: Meena (Smt) w/o Balwant Hemke vs. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to hold that mere recovery of currency notes and a positive phenolphthalein test are insufficient to establish guilt without proof of demand and acceptance.

rules.reference: Standard of proof in corruption cases
rules.relevance: The court held that demand and acceptance must be proved by cogent evidence and beyond reasonable doubt, not merely by preponderance of probabilities.

rules.case_name: Ayyasami vs. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: Ayyasami vs. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to support the requirement of corroboration for the testimony of an interested witness in corruption cases.

rules.case_name: Panna Damodar Rathi vs. State of Maharashtra
rules.reference: Panna Damodar Rathi vs. State of Maharashtra
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent for the principle that the sole testimony of an interested complainant cannot be relied upon without independent corroboration.

rules.case_name: Ram Singh vs. Col. Ram Singh
rules.reference: Ram Singh vs. Col. Ram Singh
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to establish the strict standards for admissibility of tape-recorded evidence, including voice identification and exclusion of tampering.

rules.case_name: Rizwan Ahmed Javed Shaikh & Ors. v. Jammal Patel & Ors.
rules.reference: Rizwan Ahmed Javed Shaikh & Ors. v. Jammal Patel & Ors.
rules.relevance: Cited by the majority to support the view that if an act is done while acting as a public officer in the course of the same transaction as official duty, Section 197 protection applies.

rules.case_name: Sankaran Moitra v. Sadhna Das & Anr.
rules.reference: Sankaran Moitra v. Sadhna Das & Anr.
rules.relevance: Held that sanction is a condition precedent for successful prosecution and the plea can be raised at the inception if unimpeachable circumstances show the act was in discharge of duty.

rules.case_name: Sankaran Moitra v. Sadhna Das & Anr.
rules.reference: Sankaran Moitra v. Sadhna Das & Anr.
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this case, finding it inapplicable because the specific issue of removal powers under the Jharkhand Police Manual was directly covered by the ratio in Nagraj.

rules.case_name: Sankaran Moitra vs. Sadhna Das and another
rules.reference: Sankaran Moitra vs. Sadhna Das and another
rules.relevance: The High Court relied on this case to quash proceedings, but the Supreme Court clarified that not all acts committed during investigation are official duties; the specific nature of the act must be examined.

rules.case_name: Nagraj v. State of Mysore
rules.reference: Nagraj v. State of Mysore
rules.relevance: The court relied on this precedent to hold that if a police officer can be dismissed or removed by a superior officer (like the Inspector General) without State Government sanction, then prosecution sanction under Section 197 Cr.P.C. is not required.

rules.reference: Functional Disability vs. Physical Disability
rules.relevance: A claimant suffers 100% functional disability if they lose the capacity to pursue their specific vocation, even if physical disability is less than 100%.

rules.case_name: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Mubasir Ahmed
rules.reference: National Insurance Company Ltd. v. Mubasir Ahmed
rules.relevance: Holds that loss of earning capacity is distinct from physical disablement and that 100% functional disability can exist even without 100% physical disability.

rules.case_name: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar and Ors.
rules.reference: Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar and Ors.
rules.relevance: Provides a three-step test to ascertain the effect of permanent disability on actual earning capacity, distinguishing between physical disablement and loss of earning capacity based on profession.

rules.case_name: Master Ayush v. Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Another
rules.reference: Master Ayush v. Branch Manager, Reliance General Insurance Company Limited and Another
rules.relevance: Supports the award of compensation for loss of marriage prospects and conveyance charges in cases involving severe disability and young victims.

rules.case_name: Govind Yadav v. The New India Insurance Company Ltd.
rules.reference: Govind Yadav v. The New India Insurance Company Ltd.
rules.relevance: Establishes that adequate compensation must cover physical injury, loss of earning, and inability to lead a normal life in cases of permanent disability.

rules.case_name: State of Punjab v. Bakshish Singh
rules.reference: State of Punjab v. Bakshish Singh
rules.relevance: The court distinguished this case, holding it was not an authority for invalidating dismissal based on regularization of absence, but rather concerned with procedural irregularities and the scope of remand.

rules.reference: Delhi Police Act, 1978
rules.relevance: The statutory provision under which the departmental enquiry against the appellant was initiated.

rules.case_name: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Harihar Gopal
rules.reference: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Harihar Gopal
rules.relevance: The court relied on this decision to establish that an order granting leave after termination is for maintaining correct service records and does not invalidate the earlier termination order.

rules.case_name: Sangeroid Remedies Ltd. v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.reference: Sangeroid Remedies Ltd. v. Union of India & Ors.
rules.relevance: Cited to hold that courts will not ordinarily interfere with the quantum of punishment if procedural requirements are met and misconduct is proved.

rules.case_name: Sangramsinh P Gaekwad & Ors. v. Shantadevi P Gaekwad (Dead) through LRs & Ors.
rules.reference: Sangramsinh P Gaekwad & Ors. v. Shantadevi P Gaekwad (Dead) through LRs & Ors.
rules.relevance: Cited to support the principle that judicial admissions form the foundation of rights and that a party cannot resile from admissions made in pleadings.

rules.reference: Pleading Standards in Specific Performance
rules.relevance: The court considered the principle that if a plaintiff explicitly pleads readiness and willingness in the plaint, and the defendant does not raise a contrary plea in the written statement or cross-objections, the court cannot dismiss the suit on the ground of lack of such pleading.

rules.case_name: Pushparani S. Sundaram and Ors. v. Pauline Manomani James and Ors.
rules.reference: Pushparani S. Sundaram and Ors. v. Pauline Manomani James and Ors.
rules.relevance: Clarifies that a mere plea of readiness and willingness is insufficient; it must be proved by evidence.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: Prescribes the manner in which averments of readiness and willingness are required to be made in a suit for specific performance.

rules.case_name: Ouseph Varghese v. Joseph Aley and Ors.
rules.reference: Ouseph Varghese v. Joseph Aley and Ors.
rules.relevance: Establishes that a suit for specific performance is not maintainable without pleading readiness and willingness.

rules.case_name: K.S. Vidyanadam and Ors. v. Vairavan
rules.reference: K.S. Vidyanadam and Ors. v. Vairavan
rules.relevance: Holds that even if time is not of the essence, the plaintiff must perform within a reasonable time determined by surrounding circumstances.

rules.reference: Bihar Zila Parishad Secondary and Higher Secondary Teachers (Appointment and Service Conditions) Rules, 2006
rules.relevance: The court examined these rules to determine the eligibility criteria for Librarian appointments, specifically noting the requirement of a degree from a recognized university and the ambiguity regarding distance education recognition.

rules.reference: Effect of ex post facto recognition during ongoing selection
rules.relevance: The court held that where the selection process is incomplete and recognition is granted with retrospective effect, candidates should be allowed the benefit of such recognition to prevent injustice.

rules.reference: Indira Gandhi National Open University Act, 1985
rules.relevance: Cited to establish the authority of the Distance Education Council to determine standards and grant recognition for distance education courses.

rules.reference: Eligibility conditions must be satisfied on the date of application
rules.relevance: The court acknowledged this general principle but applied it liberally due to administrative confusion and the fact that the selection process was ongoing when recognition was granted.

rules.case_name: Gujarat University v. Shri Krishna
rules.reference: Gujarat University v. Shri Krishna
rules.relevance: Established that Entry 66 List I prevails over State entries in case of overlap regarding standards in higher education.

rules.reference: Maharashtra Employees of Private Schools Rules, 1981
rules.relevance: This rule governs the filling of reserved posts. It states that if a post reserved for a specific Backward Class category cannot be filled, it may be filled by a candidate from other remaining categories in the specified order. It further states that if no person from any of the backward class categories is available, the post may be filled temporarily on a year-to-year basis by a candidate not belonging to the Backward Classes.

rules.reference: Horizontal Reservation
rules.relevance: The court applied the principle that reservations for women and sportspersons are horizontal and cut across vertical categories, meaning unfilled vacancies should be filled by suitable candidates from other categories rather than carried forward.

rules.reference: Application of merit-based exclusion from reserved quota
rules.relevance: The court held that the principle where an SC/ST candidate selected on merit is not counted against the reserved quota applies only to recruitment by open competition, not to promotions based on seniority-cum-suitability.

rules.reference: U.P. Public Services (Reservation for Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes) Act, 1994
rules.relevance: The court interpreted this section to hold that a reserved category candidate selected on merit in open competition shall not be adjusted against reserved vacancies.

rules.reference: Model 40-point roster
rules.relevance: The court relied on this rule to determine that in small cadres, if a reserved point is treated as unreserved, the reservation is carried forward to subsequent years, justifying the treatment of one 1994 vacancy as reserved.

rules.case_name: BGS SGS Soma JV v. NHPC Limited
rules.reference: BGS SGS Soma JV v. NHPC Limited
rules.relevance: Clarified that once a seat is designated (by agreement or tribunal), it acts as an exclusive jurisdiction clause. Held that when the tribunal fixes the seat under Section 20(2), it is static and cannot be changed by subsequent venue changes.

rules.case_name: Inox Renewables Ltd v. Jayesh Electricals Ltd.
rules.reference: Inox Renewables Ltd v. Jayesh Electricals Ltd.
rules.relevance: Distinguished on the basis that it involved a change of seat by mutual consent of parties under Section 20(1), whereas the present case involved a seat fixed by the arbitrator under Section 20(2).

rules.case_name: Bhartiya Aluminium Company v. Kaiser Aluminium Technical Services Inc.
rules.reference: Bhartiya Aluminium Company v. Kaiser Aluminium Technical Services Inc.
rules.relevance: Established the distinction between 'seat' (juridical centre) and 'venue' (physical location) and held that the seat determines the supervisory jurisdiction.

rules.reference: Shashoua Principle
rules.relevance: The court applied this principle to determine that where a venue is designated and governed by supranational rules (like UNCITRAL) or national arbitration laws without contrary indicia, the venue is deemed the juridical seat.

rules.reference: Juridical Seat of Arbitration
rules.relevance: The court applied the principle that the seat of arbitration determines the exclusive supervisory jurisdiction of the courts, distinct from the venue of hearings.

rules.case_name: Suman Sethi v. Ajay K. Churiwal and Anr.
rules.reference: Suman Sethi v. Ajay K. Churiwal and Anr.
rules.relevance: Established that a notice must specifically demand the cheque amount; an omnibus demand without specifying the cheque amount fails to meet legal requirements, whereas additional claims for interest or costs are severable if the cheque amount is specified.

rules.case_name: K.R. Indira v. Dr. G. Adinarayana
rules.reference: K.R. Indira v. Dr. G. Adinarayana
rules.relevance: Reinforced that a notice is imperfect if it does not specifically contain a demand for the payment of the cheque amount, as the non-payment of the cheque amount is the specific incriminating circumstance under Section 138.

rules.case_name: Central Bank of India & Anr. v. M/s. Saxons Farms & Ors.
rules.reference: Central Bank of India & Anr. v. M/s. Saxons Farms & Ors.
rules.relevance: Established that the object of the notice is to give the drawer a chance to rectify the omission; payment of the cheque amount absolves the drawer from criminal liability even if other demands are made.

rules.case_name: M. Narayanan Nambiar v. State of Kerala
rules.reference: M. Narayanan Nambiar v. State of Kerala
rules.relevance: Cited for the principle that penal statutes must be construed strictly, but also that where language is clear, it should be given its fair commonsense meaning.

rules.reference: Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881
rules.relevance: Prescribes that a complaint must be made within one month of the cause of action, but empowers the Court to take cognizance after the prescribed period if the complainant satisfies the Court of sufficient cause for the delay.

rules.reference: Indian Penal Code, 1860
rules.relevance: The sections under which the FIR was registered; the court examined whether the facts disclosed a prima facie case for cheating, forgery, and criminal conspiracy.

rules.case_name: Randheer Singh v. The State of U.P. & others
rules.reference: Randheer Singh v. The State of U.P. & others
rules.relevance: Cited to support the principle that purely civil disputes involving financial transactions should not be given the color of criminal cases.

rules.case_name: Union Bank of India vs. Satyawati Tandon
rules.reference: Union Bank of India vs. Satyawati Tandon
rules.relevance: Established the principle that High Courts should not exercise writ jurisdiction when an efficacious statutory alternative remedy is available.

rules.reference: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016
rules.relevance: Empowers the adjudicating authority to inquire into and penalize fraudulent or malicious initiation of insolvency proceedings.

rules.reference: Forum shopping and territorial jurisdiction
rules.relevance: The court condemned the practice of providing false addresses to create artificial jurisdiction in a forum convenient to the complainant but lacking legal basis.

rules.reference: Recruitment Rules / Executive Instructions
rules.relevance: The court noted that appointments to public posts must be made in terms of applicable Recruitment Rules or executive instructions, not merely based on training completion.

rules.reference: Doctrine of Past Practice and Non-Arbitrariness
rules.relevance: The court held that the State cannot apply rules differently at two different points in time to the prejudice of the same class of candidates, and that past practice must be respected to prevent injustice where candidates were previously excluded.

rules.reference: U.P. Procedure for Direct Recruitment of Group 'C' Posts (Outside the Purview of Public Service Commission) (First Amendment) Rules, 2003
rules.relevance: The court analyzed whether the merit-based selection procedure in these rules could be applied to the detriment of candidates who had been previously excluded under a different interpretation of the rules.

rules.reference: Himachal Pradesh Takniki Shiksha Board Act, 1986
rules.relevance: Established the statutory regime for recognizing institutions and awarding diplomas, which the court found was ignored by the relaxation order.

rules.reference: Uttar Pradesh Subordinate Services Selection Commission Act, 2014
rules.relevance: The court relied on this Act to establish the statutory authority of the Commission to conduct selections, overriding previous administrative rules.

rules.reference: Minor discrepancies in witness testimony
rules.relevance: The court held that minor contradictions or embellishments on trivial matters do not affect the core of the prosecution case and should not lead to rejection of evidence.

rules.case_name: A Shanker v. State of Karnataka
rules.reference: A Shanker v. State of Karnataka
rules.relevance: Cited to support the principle that normal discrepancies due to errors of observation or memory do not render evidence unreliable if they do not affect the core of the case.

rules.case_name: Modan Singh vs. State of Rajasthan
rules.reference: Evidence of Investigating Officer
rules.relevance: Observed that where the evidence of the investigating officer regarding recovery is convincing, the evidence need not be rejected even if seizure witnesses do not support the prosecution version.

rules.reference: Failure to cross-examine on material issues
rules.relevance: The court held that if a question is not put to a witness in cross-examination who could furnish an explanation, the correctness or legality of that fact/issue cannot be raised later.

rules.case_name: C. Muniappan & Ors. vs. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: Evaluation of Hostile Witness Testimony
rules.relevance: Summarizes that relevant parts of hostile witness evidence can be used and minor discrepancies do not vitiate testimony if they do not go to the heart of the matter.

rules.case_name: V Surendra Mohan v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: V Surendra Mohan v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.relevance: Distinguished as it was rendered under the old 1995 Act and lacked proper reasonable accommodation analysis.

rules.reference: United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD)
rules.relevance: Supports interpretation that failure to provide reasonable accommodation constitutes discrimination.

rules.reference: Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016
rules.relevance: Mandates non-discrimination in employment and provision of reasonable accommodation.

rules.case_name: Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
rules.reference: Jeeja Ghosh v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Established that equality involves reasonable differentiation and specific measures for substantive equality.

rules.case_name: Vikash Kumar v. Union of India
rules.reference: Vikash Kumar v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Established that confining scribe facilities only to benchmark disabilities deprives persons with genuine writing difficulties of their statutory entitlements, mandating reasonable accommodation for all specified disabilities with writing difficulties.

rules.case_name: Rekha Chaturvedi (Smt.) v. University of Rajasthan and Others
rules.reference: Rekha Chaturvedi (Smt.) v. University of Rajasthan and Others
rules.relevance: The Court relied on this precedent to affirm that an advertisement constitutes a representation to the public and the authority is bound by it, meaning candidates acquiring qualifications after the deadline cannot be considered.

rules.provision: Rules governing appointment of Head Masters
rules.reference: Rajasthan Educational Service Rules, 1970
rules.relevance: These rules prescribe the minimum qualifications, including specific educational degrees and teaching experience in higher classes, required for the post of Head Master.

rules.reference: Principle of Eligibility Date
rules.relevance: The court applied the principle that a press note allowing corrections to application forms does not shift the date of eligibility or allow ineligible candidates to become eligible.

rules.reference: Rajasthan State and Subordinate Services (Direct Recruitment by Combined Competitive Examination) Rules, 1999
rules.relevance: These rules governed the recruitment process and established the framework for eligibility criteria as of the date of application submission.

rules.reference: Rajasthan Education (Subordinate Services) Rules, 1971
rules.relevance: These rules govern the posts of Teacher Grade-III and Laboratory Assistants, establishing them as subordinate services with lower minimum educational qualifications (Matriculation/Secondary) distinct from the 1970 Rules.

rules.reference: Sports Policy of UT Chandigarh (2003)
rules.relevance: The policy defines the objective of the sports quota as promoting sports proficiency and grading candidates based on sports achievements, not academic merit.

rules.case_name: Manish Kumar v. Union of India
rules.reference: Manish Kumar v. Union of India
rules.relevance: Cited for the principle that reasonable classification requires an intelligible differentia and a rational nexus to the object sought to be achieved.

rules.case_name: A. Periakaruppan v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.reference: A. Periakaruppan v. State of Tamil Nadu
rules.relevance: The court considered this precedent regarding the assumption that non-litigating candidates may have abandoned their claims, but distinguished the facts to allow admission based on merit.

rules.case_name: Ashutosh Gupta v. State of Rajasthan
rules.reference: Ashutosh Gupta v. State of Rajasthan
rules.relevance: Cited to establish that Article 14 permits classification based on rational distinctions relevant to the subject matter.

rules.case_name: Venkateshwara Theatre v. State of A.P.
rules.reference: Venkateshwara Theatre v. State of A.P.
rules.relevance: Cited for the principle that treating unequals as equals constitutes discrimination if there is no rational relation to the object of the law.

rules.case_name: Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Ragunathpur Nafar Academy
rules.reference: Esha Bhattacharjee v. Managing Committee of Ragunathpur Nafar Academy
rules.relevance: Supported the condonation of delay in filing the appeal due to the bona fide pendency of a review petition.

rules.reference: Code of Civil Procedure, 1908
rules.relevance: These rules govern the procedure for substitution of legal representatives upon the death of a party and the consequences of failure to substitute, including abatement.

rules.case_name: A. Viswanatha Pillai v. Special Tehsildar for Land Acquisition No.4
rules.reference: A. Viswanatha Pillai v. Special Tehsildar for Land Acquisition No.4
rules.relevance: Held that one co-owner can file a suit on behalf of all co-owners, and the decree enures to the benefit of all, implying the estate is represented by the plaintiffs.

rules.case_name: Venigalla Koteswaramman v. Malempati Suryamba
rules.reference: Venigalla Koteswaramman v. Malempati Suryamba
rules.relevance: Consolidated the law on Order 22 CPC, emphasizing that abatement depends on whether the right to sue survives and the nature of the decree, requiring a factual inquiry rather than mechanical dismissal.

rules.case_name: State of Andhra Pradesh through Principal Secretary and Ors. v. Pratap Karan and Ors.
rules.reference: State of Andhra Pradesh through Principal Secretary and Ors. v. Pratap Karan and Ors.
rules.relevance: Held that non-substitution of legal representatives does not cause abatement if the estate is fully and substantially represented by other sharers.

rules.case_name: Arun Kumar v. Anita Mishra
rules.reference: Arun Kumar v. Anita Mishra
rules.relevance: Held that the dishonour of a cheque issued pursuant to a settlement agreement can give rise to a fresh cause of action under Section 138.

rules.reference: Settlement subsumes original complaint
rules.relevance: The court held that once a settlement agreement is entered into, it subsumes the original complaint, and parties cannot pursue parallel prosecutions for the same underlying transaction.

rules.case_name: HMT Watches Ltd. v. M.A. Abida
rules.reference: HMT Watches Ltd. v. M.A. Abida
